text: Research method note: WebFetch/curl egress to vendor and regulator sites (koerber-pharma.com, emerson.com, fda.gov, ecfr.gov) was blocked in this environment on 2026-09-27, so findings rest on search-engine page summaries plus domain knowledge. Entries marked verified:false are from domain knowledge and should be checked against the primary source before use.

name: Körber Werum PAS-X (MBR Design & Execution)
configurability: MBRs are drawn in a graphical designer from libraries of standardised, reusable building blocks; the tool runs automated plausibility/completeness checks on an MBR (vendor cites more than 50 check criteria) before it can progress. A Generic MBR (GMBR) concept lets one process design serve a family of similar target materials, with the per-material differences held as parameters rather than copied designs. Körber positions MBR design as a mandatory, high-effort part of every MES project and sells MBR design services and training.

text: PAS-X GMBR: one generic master batch record is shared by a group of materials with a similar process; material-specific values are modelled as parameters of the GMBR instead of creating a separate MBR per product. This is the vendor's main lever against MBR sprawl.

Körber describes the MBR as the template from which the executed electronic batch record is generated, and says it carries the input material list, applicable SOPs, detailed work instructions and process data such as IPCs, CPPs and CQAs. Implication: the MBR designer must model all of these as first-class objects, not free text.

name: Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk PharmaSuite
configurability: Recipe designer follows ISA-88 recipe design principles; authors assemble master recipes and workflows from a building-block library so a modelled item (e.g. an IPC check) is maintained once and re-used across many recipes. v5 let site recipe authors build new workflows from existing blocks without programming; v6 added predefined 'workflows' (non-order-bound procedures such as cleaning or equipment tasks) that operators pick and execute on demand, with the executed workflow data appended to and tracked in the EBR, which lets master recipes be slimmer. Automation integration collects equipment data, downloads setpoints and captures automation events into the EBR.

name: Emerson Syncade (now positioned within DeltaV MES)
configurability: Recipes are authored from 'standard recipe objects': pre-built, supported building blocks for common operations, each bundling work instructions, instruction text, behaviours and parameters, usable out of the box; the parameters an author must set are explicitly flagged and simplified. Emerson presents the standard objects as a way to impose consistent authoring conventions across recipe authors. Syncade coordinates manual electronic work instructions with automated steps run by the DCS (DeltaV), and combines document, equipment and materials management with workflow.

text: PAS-X 'Library Elements' (LEs) are reusable, customer-built building blocks that package a recurring sequence of process steps and automated decisions (the cited example bundles the steps needed to drain a vessel). An MBR embeds them by reference rather than by copy, and each reference can be given its own parameter values. Design implication: library blocks must be referenced (with version pinning and where-used tracking) and parameterised per use.

name: Siemens Opcenter Execution Pharma
configurability: Authorised users design MBRs graphically, with central parameter management and re-usable sub-process libraries; the executed eBR for each production order is generated automatically from the approved MBR. Native MES-DCS integration (SIMATIC PCS 7/neo) lets automated phases and manual instructions live in one MBR. Recent releases (2411, 2505, 2511, 2605) add a web-based Operator Cockpit, modular weighing functions, tighter data-integrity controls and (2605) AI-assisted design of workflows, forms and checks.

name: MasterControl Manufacturing Excellence (Mx)
configurability: No-code 'builder' in which production record templates are assembled from typed 'phase steps'; each phase step type exposes its own formatting and behaviour utilities. Global elements (shared data such as materials, equipment, reusable content) are held centrally so an update is made once and propagated. Covers EBR/eDHR, e-logbooks and asset management; records are issued from an approved template.

name: Apprentice.io Tempo
configurability: No-code drag-and-drop procedure templates (types include batch record, general method, SOP, test method) with branching logic, validation rules and reusable templates; batch parameters and parameter groups let one template serve multiple products or variants. Templates move through a five-stage lifecycle (draft, in review, pending approval, approved, effective); an effective version is locked and changes require a new draft version. An AI 'authoring agent' can convert PDF procedures into draft digital records. Notably, a template-level setting can switch off review/approval so a template jumps from draft to effective, intended to speed system testing.

name: Tulip (Frontline Operations Platform, GxP edition)
configurability: General-purpose no-code app builder (steps, widgets, triggers, tables) used to build eBR apps. Each app version must collect the configured set of electronic approvals before it can be published; publishing freezes the app logic, and multiple published versions can coexist. A Developer Mode runs apps for testing without writing Table records or completion records to the production database (test data lives only in the browser tab). Platform provides audit trail, unique accounts/roles and Part 11 style e-signatures, but GMP-specific semantics (weighing, reconciliation, IPC statistics) must be built by the customer, which pushes validation effort toward Category 5 style for the app logic.

text: Tempo documents a template-level switch that bypasses review/approval so a draft can become effective immediately for system testing. In a general eBR this must be guarded: an unapproved (test) master must be technically incapable of producing a GMP batch record, e.g. by restricting such masters to a non-GMP test/sandbox mode or environment and watermarking their records.

Tulip's Developer Mode pattern (test executions of an unreleased app that never write to production tables or completion records) is a concrete precedent for an MBR 'test run' capability that verifies configuration without contaminating GMP data.

MBR sprawl is a recognised problem: Werum introduced Generic MBRs in 2012 specifically because packaging generates huge numbers of near-identical MBRs that differ only in parameter values (e.g. pack count, leaflet language, packaging material). Design implication: separate process structure (the generic master) from product/variant parameter sets, so a variant is a parameter set, not a copied MBR.

Körber ships pre-built 'content packages' (PAS-X Content Suite: administration templates, process libraries, integration libraries, equipment libraries; reported as 16 packages) including 'MBR Design Elements' templates for recurring process fragments such as granulation, IPC testing and reconciliation, curated with the user community. A general system benefits from shipping a vendor-validated starter library of blocks per dosage form, clearly separated from customer-authored blocks.

PAS-X runs automated plausibility and completeness checks on an MBR during design (more than 50 check criteria), for example flagging a recipe whose required process setpoints are missing, before the MBR enters electronic role-based review and approval. This is a pattern of 'static verification' of configuration that a general system should provide as a gating step before approval.

Emerson added automated transfer of product recipes, material master data and configuration settings between environments (design/development, validation, production) because manually re-verifying that production matches the tested configuration was slow. Design implication: MBRs and their dependent master data should be exportable as a signed, versioned package whose content hash is checked on import, so the object verified in test is provably the object released in production.

Syncade recipes visually distinguish manual steps executed through MES electronic work instructions from automated steps executed by the DCS, within the same procedure. A general MBR model needs a step attribute for execution mode (manual, semi-automated, automated/equipment-executed) with different data-capture and signature rules per mode.

PharmaSuite master recipes follow ISA-88/95 and ship a standard building-block set said to cover EBR for API, biotech, bulk manufacturing and packaging; IPC checks modelled in the building-block library are maintained once and reused across recipes; master recipe maintenance provides central storage with revision control.

ISA-88 procedural control model is a four-level hierarchy: a recipe procedure is an ordered set of unit procedures, each an ordered set of operations, each an ordered set of phases; the phase is the smallest procedural element (e.g. open a valve, start an agitator, read a gauge). Mapping for a configurable eBR: Procedure = whole MBR; Unit procedure = stage bound to one unit/room/equipment train (e.g. dispensing, granulation, compression, filling); Operation = coherent processing activity within that stage (e.g. wet massing); Phase = the typed building block (weigh, charge, record parameter, sample, verify, timer, etc.).

ISA-88 recipe types: general (enterprise, equipment-independent), site (site-specific, still equipment-independent, adapted for local materials/language), master (tied to an equipment class/process cell, contains the product-specific information needed to make a batch) and control (a copy of the master instantiated for one batch, to which batch-specific information such as batch ID, output lot ID and the actual equipment units is added). Mapping: approved MBR version = master recipe; each issued eBR = control recipe; an optional 'generic/process template' layer corresponds to general/site recipes.

ISA-88 recipe content is split into header (identity, version, status, product), formula (process inputs with quantities, process parameters, expected outputs), equipment requirements (constraints on which equipment class/capability may be used) and procedure. A configurable MBR should keep these as separate structures so that the same procedure can be bound to different formula sets (variants, batch sizes) and equipment can be expressed as a class requirement resolved to a specific unit only at execution.

ISA-88 notes a control recipe can be created from the master fully automatically, semi-automatically, or with manual operator input. For GMP, creation of the executed record (control recipe) from the approved MBR should be automatic and exact (21 CFR 211.188(a) expects an accurate reproduction of the master, checked; automation replaces the manual check by a validated copy mechanism plus a content hash), with only batch-specific values (batch number, batch size within approved range, actual equipment, dates) supplied at issuance.

ISA-88 Part 2 (S88.02) defines the Procedure Function Chart (PFC) notation for depicting procedural logic (sequence, parallel/simultaneous branches, alternative/selective branches, loops, synchronisation) in master and control recipes; Part 3 (2003) models equipment-independent general/site recipes; Part 4 (2006) gives an object model for batch production records (materials used and produced, activities performed, environment in which the batch ran). A configurable MBR designer can adopt PFC semantics for its flow graph and Part 4 as the reference structure of the executed record.

Practical mapping caveat (domain knowledge): classic ISA-88 was designed for automated batch control of process cells, while most solid-dose, packaging and aseptic eBR content is manual or semi-manual work instructions. Vendors therefore reuse the hierarchy for structure and reuse, but extend the 'phase' concept into typed manual building blocks (weighing, identification, verification, sampling, data capture), and treat equipment-executed phases (DCS/PLC) as one block type that exchanges setpoints and results with Level 2.

ISA-95 boundaries for a configurable eBR (Level 3 MES/MOM): ERP (Level 4) owns item master, BOM/formula at business level, process orders and inventory valuation, and receives production performance (consumptions, yields, goods receipts) back; Level 2 (DCS/SCADA/PLC, weigh scales, lyophilizers, sterilizers) receives setpoints/recipes and returns process values, alarms and cycle reports; LIMS owns QC test results and specifications; QMS owns deviations, CAPA and change control; DMS owns SOPs. The eBR should own the MBR, execution, in-process data and the batch record, and interface through ISA-95 style objects (B2MML: product definition, production schedule, production performance, material/equipment/personnel models).

FDA Computer Software Assurance guidance status: draft issued Sept 2022; finalised by CDRH/CBER on 24 Sept 2025 (docket FDA-2022-D-0795), superseding Section 6 of the 2002 General Principles of Software Validation; then reissued on 3 Feb 2026 as 'Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality Management System Software' to align terminology with the device QMSR (21 CFR 820 incorporating ISO 13485), which took effect 2 Feb 2026. The Feb 2026 version is reported as the current one.

CSA scope caveat for a drug eBR: the guidance is formally written for medical device production and quality system software (21 CFR 820) and is not a CDER drug CGMP guidance, although it was developed in consultation with CDER and industry widely applies its principles to 21 CFR 211.68 systems. A drug-product eBR should therefore cite 211.68, Part 11 and Annex 11 as the binding basis, and use CSA only as supporting rationale for risk-based, least-burdensome assurance (scaling rigour to process risk, accepting unscripted/exploratory testing and supplier evidence for lower-risk functions).

CSA risk logic: features whose failure could compromise product quality or patient safety are 'high process risk' and warrant more rigorous (often scripted) assurance; others can be assured with unscripted methods (ad hoc, error guessing, exploratory, scenario-based) and leveraged supplier testing, with records kept of the approach and outcome. For an eBR platform: engine-level guardrails (limit checks, e-signature binding, status checks, calculation engine, record generation) are high process risk; UI layout, report cosmetics and convenience features are not.

GAMP 5 Second Edition (ISPE, July 2022) keeps the software categories (1 infrastructure, 3 standard non-configured, 4 configured, 5 custom) but stresses they form a continuum and are not a checklist, and puts critical thinking by SMEs, supplier leverage, cloud/SaaS and agile delivery at the centre. A configurable eBR platform is a Category 4 configured product; customer MBRs built only from vendor-supplied typed blocks are configuration, whereas customer-authored scripts, free-form formulas or custom code blocks move that element toward Category 5 and need correspondingly deeper verification.

EU GMP revision status: drafts of a rewritten Annex 11 (grown from ~5 to ~19 pages in 17 sections, adding explicit expectations on audit trail setup and review, identity and access management, e-signatures incl. hybrid solutions, supplier oversight and cybersecurity), a revised Chapter 4 (Documentation) and a new Annex 22 (Artificial Intelligence) were published 7 July 2025 with consultation closing 7 Oct 2025; finals were expected from mid-2026 with operative dates set in the final texts. Final publication could not be confirmed in this research (see open question). Design to the draft now, since it is the direction of travel.

The Annex 11 revision concept paper took the position that users must be unable to alter audit trail entries or switch the audit trail off; commentators read the July 2025 draft as making audit trails mandatory and not switchable off by normal users. This supports treating audit trail as a non-configurable guardrail in an eBR (no tenant, site, MBR or admin setting to disable it).

Has the European Commission published the FINAL revised EU GMP Annex 11, Chapter 4 and new Annex 22 (drafts of 7 July 2025) by Sept 2026, and what are the operative dates? Searches on 2026-09-27 only returned 'expected mid-2026' statements; verify on health.ec.europa.eu (EudraLex Volume 4) before freezing requirements.

Does FDA CDER intend to issue a drug-CGMP counterpart to the device CSA guidance (Feb 2026 version), or reference it in a revised Part 11 / computerized systems guidance? Until then, CSA is persuasive but not binding for 21 CFR 211 eBR validation.

FDA's Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A (final, Dec 2018) treats a workflow such as creating an electronic master production and control record as an intended use that must itself be validated; qualifying the platform alone does not show that a given electronic MPCR has correct calculations and behaves properly. This is the direct FDA basis for a two-tier strategy: validate the configurable platform once (Cat 4), then verify every MBR configuration (its calculations, limits, flow and signatures) before approval.

The same FDA Q&A expects controls so that changes to computerised MPCRs (and other records) can be made only by authorised personnel, and discourages shared logins because actions must be attributable to individuals. For a configurable eBR this means MBR authoring rights, MBR approval rights and execution rights are separate permissions, every configuration change is audit-trailed with user identity, and generic/shared accounts are technically impossible.

USP General Notices 7.20 (Rounding Rules): an observed or calculated value is rounded to the number of decimal places in the limit expression, looking only at the single digit to the right of the last place of the limit (below 5 drop it; 5 or above increment the preceding digit, i.e. round-half-up, not banker's rounding); rounding happens only once the reportable value is final, and unrounded values must be carried into any further calculation even if an intermediate is displayed rounded. The calculation engine must therefore keep full precision internally, attach rounding rules to the comparison against a limit rather than to the stored value, and store both raw and rounded reportable values.

Ph. Eur. General Notices: when judging compliance with a numerical limit, the calculated result is first rounded to the number of significant figures given in the limit unless the monograph says otherwise, and limits are significant to their last stated digit (so 0.15 has two significant figures, 140 has three). The engine therefore needs a per-limit precision attribute (decimal places or significant figures) and a pharmacopoeia-selectable rounding policy; the two compendia agree on the half-up digit rule.

FDA draft guidance 'Considerations for Complying With 21 CFR 211.110' (4 Jan 2025, FRAME initiative; applies to drug products and biologics, not APIs) addresses in-process sampling and testing including advanced manufacturing and process models; FDA's view is that a control strategy relying only on a current process model would not satisfy 211.110 because model assumptions may not hold during unplanned disturbances. For an eBR: IPC blocks must support in-line/at-line/PAT data sources as well as manual tests, but model-predicted values should be recorded as such and not silently substitute for required physical sampling/testing.

rule: Audit trail is always on for every GMP-relevant create, modify, delete, sign, status change and configuration change (MBR design, library blocks, master data, roles, limits, execution data, review/release). No tenant, site, MBR, role or administrator setting can disable, pause, filter at capture time, edit or purge it.
why: Audit trail is the evidence that records were not altered without trace; if it could be configured off, no configuration of the product could be trusted. The Annex 11 revision concept paper explicitly says it should not be possible to deactivate audit trail functionality or edit its data.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(e); EU GMP Annex 11 section 9 (and 2025 draft section 12); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: Original values are never overwritten or deleted. A correction creates a new value version linked to the original, with who/when/why (reason mandatory), and the original stays visible in the record and in review views; 'delete' of GMP data is replaced by invalidation with reason.
why: Part 11 requires that record changes not obscure previously recorded information; EU Chapter 4 requires alterations to be signed, dated and to leave the original readable, with a reason where appropriate; Annex 11 requires the reason for change or deletion of GMP data to be documented.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(e); EU GMP Chapter 4 (alterations to entries); EU GMP Annex 11 section 9

rule: All GMP timestamps come from a synchronised, server-side trusted time source (stored in UTC with the site's offset); client device clocks and user-typed dates are never used as the time of an action. User-entered event times (e.g. 'time the autoclave cycle started' from a printout) are stored as data fields distinct from the system timestamp of entry.
why: Audit trails must be computer-generated and time-stamped and signatures must carry date and time; contemporaneity and sequence checks (hold times, time limits) are meaningless if the clock can be manipulated from the client.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(e), 11.50(a)(2); EU GMP Annex 11 sections 9 and 14; 21 CFR 211.111

rule: Every electronic signature shows the signer's printed name, the date/time and the meaning of signing (e.g. performed, verified, reviewed, approved, released), and is cryptographically bound to the exact content signed (e.g. hash of the step result and its context) so it cannot be removed, copied or transferred to another record; any later change to signed content invalidates or supersedes the signature visibly.
why: Signature manifestation and signature/record linking are explicit Part 11 requirements; Annex 11 requires e-signatures to be permanently linked to their record and to include time and date.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70; EU GMP Annex 11 section 14

rule: Signing requires at least two distinct identification components (user ID + password) or a biometric; the first signing in a continuous controlled session uses all components and later signings at least the private component; signings outside a continuous session re-use all components. Configuration may make this stricter (e.g. always full re-authentication, MFA), never weaker; no 'remember my signature' or pre-signing.
why: Minimum e-signature component rules are regulatory; weaker settings would make every signature in every configured MBR non-compliant.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.200(a), 11.300; EU GMP Annex 11 section 14

rule: Only unique, individually assigned user accounts can perform GMP actions; shared, generic or service accounts cannot sign, execute steps or approve. Accounts are never deleted or reassigned to another person (disable only), so historical attribution survives.
why: Attributability; FDA discourages shared logins because actions cannot be traced to a person; e-signatures must be unique to one individual and not reused or reassigned.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.100(a), 11.10(d); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018); EU GMP Annex 11 section 12

rule: Authority checks are evaluated by the engine at the moment of each action: the user must hold a role permitted for that action on that step type/MBR/site AND (where configured as a prerequisite) have current training on the governing document/MBR version; failing checks block the action rather than warn.
why: Part 11 requires authority checks so that only authorised individuals can sign, alter records or perform the operation; 211.25 requires personnel to have training for their assigned functions.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(g), 11.10(i); 21 CFR 211.25; EU GMP Chapter 2; Annex 11 section 12

rule: For any step configured with a verification (second-person check/witness), the verifier must be a different authenticated individual from the performer (and from any other signer that the step's segregation rule excludes); the engine rejects same-user verification regardless of role or admin rights. Manual component charge-in and manual yield calculation always carry mandatory independent verification; the only permitted reduction to single-person verification is when the operation itself was performed by qualified automated equipment and one person checks that it did so correctly.
why: 211.101(d) and 211.103 require a second person for manual charge-in and yield calculations and 211.68(c) allows automated equipment to substitute for the performer only; 211.188(b) requires identification of persons performing and checking each significant step. A verifier identical to the performer is no verification at all.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(c)-(d), 211.103, 211.68(c), 211.188(b)(11); EU GMP Chapter 4 (batch processing record: initials of operator and, where appropriate, of the person checking)

rule: MBR (master record) lifecycle is fixed: authored by one person, independently checked by a second person, and approved by the quality unit before it can become effective; author, checker and QA approver must be distinct users; approval signatures cannot be configured away (no 'skip review' switch for GMP masters). Customers may ADD reviewers/approvers to the route, not remove the minimum.
why: 211.186(a) requires the master record to be prepared and signed by one person and independently checked and signed by a second; 211.100(a) and 211.22 require quality unit approval of production procedures and changes to them. A vendor option to bypass review for testing must be confined to non-GMP use.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.186(a), 211.100(a), 211.22(c); EU GMP Chapter 4 (approval of manufacturing formula and processing instructions)

rule: A GMP batch record can only be issued from an MBR version in Effective status, for a product/site/batch size within that version's approved scope; the issued record is an exact, hash-verified instantiation of that version (plus batch-specific header values). Later MBR edits never change records already issued; retiring or superseding an MBR is a new controlled version, not an in-place edit.
why: The batch record must be an accurate reproduction of the approved master, with transcription error designed out; changes to master records must be instituted only by authorised personnel under control.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.188(a), 211.186, 211.68(b), 211.100(a); EU GMP Chapter 4 (batch processing record based on the approved formula/instructions, method avoiding transcription errors)

rule: The execution engine enforces the step sequence, prerequisites and branch conditions defined in the MBR (operational system checks). A user cannot execute a step whose predecessors are incomplete, re-order steps, or skip a mandatory step; the only way around the defined flow is a documented exception (deviation/unplanned event) approved in the system, which is itself part of the record.
why: Part 11 requires system checks that make the software keep steps and events in their allowed order; 211.100(b) requires procedures to be followed and deviations recorded and justified.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(f), 211.100(b); EU GMP Chapter 5; EU GMP Chapter 4 (deviations with signed authorisation)

rule: Data are captured contemporaneously: the step result is committed with the server time of entry; the UI offers no way to set an earlier time for the action. Late entries (e.g. recorded after an offline period or after the event) are allowed only as explicitly flagged late entries with reason and are highlighted for review.
why: Procedures must be documented at the time of performance; EU Chapter 4 requires records to be made or completed when each action is taken. Backdating is a classic data integrity failure.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(b), 211.188; EU GMP Chapter 4 (records completed at time of action); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: A value outside its approved limits is always stored exactly as entered or acquired, flagged, and routed to the exception workflow; the operator cannot suppress the flag, and re-entering a new value creates a correction (with reason and the original preserved) rather than replacing the failing result. Whether an exception becomes a formal deviation is a QA decision recorded in the system, never a configuration shortcut.
why: Unexplained discrepancies and failures to meet specifications must be investigated (211.192); deviations must be recorded and justified (211.100(b)); testing into compliance by overwriting is a data integrity violation.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(b), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 1 and Chapter 4 (deviations); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: Material status and identity are checked by the engine at dispensing and charge-in: only lots in released/approved status, within expiry or retest date, of the item (and grade/supplier where specified) called for by the MBR can be used; quarantined, rejected, expired or blocked lots and wrong items are hard-blocked (no operator override). Identity is confirmed by scanning a system-generated container/lot label, not by typing.
why: Components must be withheld from use until released by the quality unit and used only within retest/expiry; wrong-material and status errors are the main mix-up risk the eBR exists to prevent.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.84(a), 211.87, 211.80, 211.101(a)-(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (starting materials released by QC; status of materials)

rule: Equipment/room status is checked by the engine before use: the unit must belong to the equipment class required by the MBR, be qualified, within calibration and preventive maintenance due dates, in 'clean' status for the right product/cleaning type and within its clean-hold time, and not in use by another batch; failures block the step. The equipment's unique ID is recorded automatically in the batch record and its logbook.
why: Major equipment identity must be recorded in the batch record; equipment must be cleaned, maintained and calibrated per written programmes and use must be logged.

text: Scope note (2026-09-27 scope change): the product is two independent editions, TABLETS and INJECTABLES, each customisable only within its own dosage form. Building blocks below carry an 'edition' tag: 'both' = generic block needed in each edition (weighing, line clearance, signatures, calculations, flow control), 'tablets' or 'injectables' = domain-specific block shipped only in that edition. Research on how configuration works (vendor designers, ISA-88, expression language, guardrails, GAMP 5/CSA, pitfalls) applies unchanged to each edition.

Recommended meaning of 'customisable within the TABLETS edition': a customer can model any oral tablet product and process route by composing unit procedures from a closed, vendor-validated tablet library (dispensing; sieving/delumping; dry mixing; wet granulation high-shear or fluid-bed; drying; dry granulation by roller compaction or slugging; milling; final blending/lubrication; compression incl. single-layer, bilayer/multilayer and core-coated; coating incl. aqueous/solvent film, sugar and functional/enteric; imprinting/laser marking; primary packaging in blisters, bottles or strips; secondary packaging and serialisation), then setting formula, batch-size range, parameters, limits, IPC plans, equipment classes, labels and approval routes. Customers can build their own library elements (parameterised sequences) from these blocks but cannot add new primitive block types, scripts or code, and blocks with no tablet use (filter integrity, sterilisation cycles, lyophilisation, Grade A interventions) are simply absent.

Recommended meaning of 'customisable within the INJECTABLES edition': a customer can model any sterile injectable route (aseptic filling in isolator/RABS/conventional cleanroom; terminal moist-heat sterilisation; lyophilisation; solutions, suspensions/emulsions and sterile powders; vials, ampoules, cartridges and prefilled syringes incl. ready-to-use nested components; small and large volume; small molecules and biologics) from a closed library covering component preparation, compounding, bioburden sampling, sterile filtration with integrity testing, sterilisation/depyrogenation, aseptic filling and closing, lyophilisation, capping/crimping, terminal sterilisation, 100% visual inspection, CCI testing, labelling/packaging. Customer-configurable content is what the Contamination Control Strategy and validation define per site (time-limit values, EM locations and frequencies, validated cycle IDs, filter types and test parameters, intervention lists, AQL plans), while Annex 1-derived controls (e.g. PUPSIT/post-use integrity tests, time-limit enforcement, qualified-operator checks, missing-stopper rejection before capping, 100% inspection) are engine rules that can be marked not-applicable only by referencing an approved risk assessment and QA approval of the MBR.

Edition boundary also applies to master data and vocabularies, not just blocks: the tablets edition needs tablet-specific equipment classes (granulators, fluid-bed dryers, roller compactors, mills, blenders/IBCs, rotary presses with tooling sets, coaters, deduster/metal detectors, blister/bottle lines) and IPC test types (weight, breaking force, thickness, friability, disintegration, LOD, coating weight gain, leak test), whereas the injectables edition needs cleanroom grades A-D, isolator/RABS, autoclave/SIP/depyrogenation tunnel/lyophiliser/filling line classes, filter and single-use assembly types, EM sample types and visual inspection defect libraries. A shared kernel (identity, audit trail, e-signature, calculation engine, material/equipment status, exception handling, review-by-exception, record generation) should be byte-identical in both editions so that compliance guardrails cannot diverge; if the two products are built independently, a single validated kernel version should still be used or the guardrail behaviour will drift.

name: Instruction and acknowledgement
purpose: Present an approved work instruction (text, parameter values, diagrams, safety/PPE notes, link to governing SOP) and capture that the operator read it or performed it.
config_options: rich text with placeholders bound to formula/process parameters
controlled images, diagrams or video from a versioned media library
acknowledgement type: read-only vs confirm-performed
signature level: none, performer, performer plus verifier
link to governing SOP/document number
approved translations per language
display conditions (e.g. only for first batch of campaign)
engine_enforced_rules: text and media are rendered only from the approved MBR version; nothing can be edited at run time
placeholders resolve from bound, approved parameters, never from free text typed at execution
acknowledgement stored with authenticated user and server timestamp
SOP link resolves to the version effective at execution and that version number is written into the record
translations are part of the approved MBR version; changing a translation requires a new MBR version
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(a)-(b) and 211.186(b)(9) (complete manufacturing and control instructions); EU GMP Chapter 4 (processing instructions)

name: Numeric data entry / process parameter record
purpose: Record a measured or observed numeric value (process parameter, reading, count) with its unit and evaluate it against approved limits.
config_options: label and parameter code
data type (decimal/integer) and unit from the controlled UoM catalogue
precision as decimal places or significant figures
target plus tiered limits (alert/action or in-process/acceptance), inclusive or exclusive bounds
criticality class (CPP, KPP, non-critical)
allowed sources: device, automation, manual
verification requirement
permit not-applicable (with reason) or not
mandatory comment when out of limit
engine_enforced_rules: value stored with its unit at the precision entered; conversions only via the UoM service with dimension checking
limit comparison uses the compendial rounding rule attached to the limit, not a rounded stored value
out-of-limit values are kept, flagged and raise an exception; they can't be silently replaced
manual entry of a value classed as critical requires an accuracy check (second-person verification, double entry or device capture); the configuration can pick which one but cannot pick none
corrections preserve the original and require a reason
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 11 sections 5 and 6 (built-in checks, accuracy check of critical manually entered data); 21 CFR 211.188(b); 21 CFR 11.10(e)

name: Choice, pass/fail and checklist
purpose: Capture categorical observations (yes/no, pass/fail, selection from a controlled list) singly or as a checklist.
config_options: controlled value set per question
expected (passing) answer(s)
single vs multi-select
per-item comment or photo on unexpected answer
checklist item library reuse
signature/verification per item or per checklist
engine_enforced_rules: no answer is pre-filled or defaulted; each item needs a positive act by the user
an unexpected answer raises an exception and blocks dependent steps as configured
each checklist item is stored individually with its answer, not as a single 'all OK' flag
value sets are versioned master data; the record stores the value, not a pointer that could later change meaning
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(b), 211.188(b); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on attributable and contemporaneous records

name: Free text and date/time entry
purpose: Capture observations, remarks and externally sourced event times (e.g. time printed on an instrument ticket) that do not fit a structured field.
config_options: maximum length, mandatory/optional
controlled phrase suggestions
date/time format and time zone display
plausibility window for entered event times (e.g. between step start and now)
engine_enforced_rules: user-entered event times are stored as data and never replace the server timestamp of the entry
entered dates in the future or outside the batch window are rejected
MBR design check warns when free text is used where a structured, limit-checked field exists (to avoid 'paper on glass')
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(e); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5; EU GMP Chapter 4

name: Automated equipment phase / Level-2 data exchange
purpose: Invoke or supervise an equipment-executed phase (DCS/PLC/SCADA/skid) in ISA-88 terms: send setpoints from the approved formula, start/confirm the phase, and collect actual values, totals, events and alarms into the record.
config_options: equipment class and Level-2 phase or recipe identifier
mapping of formula/process parameters to setpoint tags
values to collect (actuals, totals, min/max over window, end-of-phase report)
sampling interval and time window
acceptance limits on collected values
alarm/event classes to import and which require review
manual fallback sub-procedure if interface is down (optional)
engine_enforced_rules: setpoints come only from approved formula values (or operator edits inside an approved range, verified); downloads are read back and compared before start
every imported value keeps provenance: source system, tag, device ID, source timestamp
interface loss, stale data or read-back mismatch raises an exception; fallback to manual entry is allowed only via the MBR-defined fallback path and is flagged in the record
when automation performed the operation, one person confirms correct performance; that confirmation is mandatory
alarms configured as review-relevant cannot be dropped from the review-by-exception report
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(a)-(c) (automatic equipment; input/output checked for accuracy; one-person check of automated operation); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5 (checks on data exchanged electronically between systems); ISA-88/ISA-95 Level 2-3 boundary

name: Weighing and dispensing (gravimetric)
purpose: Dispense a component into labelled containers for a specific batch to a calculated target within tolerance, with scale integration and status checks.
config_options: item and target source (formula line after scaling/potency adjustment)
tolerance absolute or relative, symmetric or asymmetric
method: net with tare, gross, weigh-by-difference, multi-container accumulation, whole-container issue
allowed scale classes / booths; minimum-weight rules
lot selection policy (FEFO/FIFO proposal, override with reason)
environmental prerequisites for the booth
container type and label template
verification: second person or automated-equipment single check
engine_enforced_rules: lot must be released, unexpired/within retest, correct item; identity confirmed by scanning the source container

scale must be calibrated, have a passed periodic performance check, and suit the target (target at or above the scale's minimum weight; readability fine enough for the tolerance) otherwise the step is blocked
weight captured from the scale interface; manual keying only via flagged fallback with mandatory verification
label generated from system data (content per 211.101(b), plus a unique container ID); no handwritten or typed labels
out-of-tolerance weight can't be accepted without exception; the accumulated quantity per item is reconciled against the target

second-person examination of each dispensed container (released status, correct weight, correct identification) unless weighing was done by qualified automated equipment, in which case one person checks
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(a)-(c), 211.68, 211.84, 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (dispensing of starting materials); USP <41>/<1251> balance minimum weight concept for analytical balances

name: Volumetric or flow-metered liquid dispensing
purpose: Dispense or transfer liquids (granulating fluid, solvents, coating liquids, WFI, bulk solution) by volume or mass with optional density/temperature conversion.
config_options: measurement principle: flow meter totaliser, calibrated vessel, load cell
conversion by density (from specification, lot CoA or measured) and temperature compensation
tolerance
source point (tank, WFI use point, container) and destination
verification requirement
engine_enforced_rules: conversions performed only by the calculation engine with dimensional checking (volume x density = mass)
meter/load cell calibration status checked before use
totaliser values read from the device where interfaced; manual readings flagged and verified
density value source recorded (spec constant vs lot-specific vs measured)
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(b)-(c), 211.68; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Material identification and charge-in
purpose: Add dispensed components (or intermediates) to the right equipment in the right order and prove each container was added once to the right batch.
config_options: charge list derived from dispensing or formula
sequence: strict order, free order within a group, or parallel
target equipment/vessel
partial charges and rinse/transfer steps
addition rate or time constraints
verification rule
engine_enforced_rules: each container is scanned; it must belong to this batch and this charge step and not be already consumed
status and expiry are re-checked at the point of use
the step cannot complete until every required container is charged or explicitly handled via exception
manual charge-in requires a different second person to verify; only automated addition reduces this to a single verifying person

name: Formula scaling and quantity adjustment
purpose: Compute batch-specific quantities from the approved formula: scale to actual batch size and adjust for lot potency/assay, water or LOD, salt-to-base factor, and compensating excipient.
config_options: approved batch-size range and scaling rule per line (proportional, fixed, stepwise)
adjustment basis per active (as-is, anhydrous, dried basis, free base)
source attribute for lot values (CoA/LIMS result fields)
compensating item (q.s. filler) and its allowed range
rounding to dispensing resolution
engine_enforced_rules: actual batch size must lie within the approved range of the MBR version
lot-specific values are pulled from quality-approved results, never typed
formulas come from the validated expression library; the computation trace (inputs, versions, result) is stored
compensating adjustments cannot drive any item outside its approved range; total batch mass is re-checked
result is verified by a second person or covered by validated automated calculation plus one-person check
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(a), 211.186(b)(3)-(4), 211.68(b); EU GMP Chapter 4 (manufacturing formula)

name: Equipment identification and status check
purpose: Bind a specific equipment unit (or train) to the step and prove it is fit for use; update its logbook automatically.
config_options: required equipment class and capabilities (e.g. working-volume range, tooling type)
list of permitted units or any unit of the class
checks to apply: cleaning status and type (e.g. product-change vs same-product clean), clean-hold expiry, calibration, qualification, preventive maintenance, open work orders
start of dirty-hold timer on release
attributes to record (e.g. line speed setting, change parts)
engine_enforced_rules: unit must be of the required class; wrong class or a failed status check blocks the step
unit ID is written to the batch record and a use entry (product, batch, time, user) to the equipment logbook automatically
a unit in use by another batch or in 'dirty' or 'maintenance' status cannot be bound
after use the unit goes to 'dirty' and its dirty-hold clock starts from server time

name: Room/line status and line clearance
purpose: Confirm, before starting (and at the end of) an operation, that the room/line is free of previous product, documents and printed materials and is in the right status.
config_options: checklist template per room/line type and operation (processing vs packaging)
photo evidence per item
automatic display of previous product/batch in that room/line
performer, verifier and optional QA verification
start-of-batch, end-of-batch and changeover triggers
engine_enforced_rules: steps located in a room/line cannot start until clearance is recorded and verified by a different person
any failed item blocks start and raises an exception
previous product/batch is filled in by the system, not typed
clearance status resets when the batch ends or another batch occupies the room/line
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.130(e) (inspection of packaging and labeling facilities immediately before use, documented in batch record), 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (line clearance before packaging and processing)

name: Environmental condition check
purpose: Verify room conditions (temperature, RH, differential pressure, particles) before and/or during a step, from a monitoring system or manual reading.
config_options: parameters and limits per room class/product need (e.g. low RH for moisture-sensitive or effervescent tablets; pressure cascades for cleanrooms)
source: BMS/EMS integration or manual instrument
timing: before start, periodic, or the full step window
action on excursion (block, exception only)
engine_enforced_rules: integrated values carry source timestamp and instrument ID; manual readings are flagged and verified
for window checks the engine pulls the excursion log for the exact step interval and attaches it for review
an excursion always generates an exception; configuration can only choose whether it also blocks
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.42, 211.46; EU GMP Chapter 3; EU GMP Annex 1 (for sterile)

name: Sampling (QC, IPC, retain, micro, stability)
purpose: Take defined samples with unique IDs, labels and chain of custody, and trigger or link laboratory testing.
config_options: sample type and purpose
quantity, container and number of samples
sampling point: location, time or event (start/middle/end, per container, per n units)
sampling plan reference (e.g. stratified locations)
label template
LIMS test/specification mapping
hand-over and receipt confirmation
engine_enforced_rules: system-generated unique sample IDs and labels; the source container/location is scanned
sampler, time and quantity recorded; sample quantity flows into yield/reconciliation
test requests sent to LIMS automatically and results returned against the sample ID
missing or late samples appear as exceptions at batch review

name: In-process control test with repeated readings and statistics
purpose: Generic IPC container for n readings per sample/time point with computed statistics and multi-tier acceptance rules (the tablet and injectable IPC blocks specialise it).
config_options: test type and method reference
n readings per sample, grouping by time point/station/side/nozzle
individual limits absolute or relative to the computed mean
statistics to compute (mean, SD, RSD, min, max, range, counts outside tiers)
acceptance rule types: mean within limits; individuals within limits; at most k outside tier 1 and none outside tier 2
instrument integration
retest rule reference (only per approved procedure)
engine_enforced_rules: statistics computed by the validated engine at full precision; rounding only for comparison/display
every reading retained; excluding a reading needs documented invalidation with reason and verification
a failing result raises an exception; a retest never replaces the original result
instrument ID and calibration status recorded with device-captured readings
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)-(b) (in-process specifications from process average/variability with suitable statistics), 211.160, 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 4 (IPC results in batch record); Ph. Eur. 2.9.5 (tiered relative-to-mean limits)

name: Calculation
purpose: Derive a value (e.g. yield, potency-adjusted amount, weight gain, mean) from recorded data and master data using the approved expression language.
config_options: expression in the sandboxed expression language referencing named inputs
output unit and precision/rounding policy
limits on the result
whether the formula is displayed to the user
verification requirement where not covered by validated automation
engine_enforced_rules: deterministic, side-effect-free evaluation; no scripts, I/O or network access
design-time unit/dimension check and dependency-graph cycle detection
full precision for intermediates; rounding only at limit comparison/reporting
if an input is corrected, the result is recomputed, the old result is preserved and dependent steps are flagged for re-verification
no manual override of a computed value
calculation trace (inputs, versions, output) stored
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(b) (formulas/input-output checked for accuracy), 211.103; EU GMP Annex 11 sections 5-6; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on validating MPCR calculations

name: Timer, hold time and time-limit enforcement
purpose: Measure and enforce minimum and maximum elapsed times between any two recorded events, within a step, across unit procedures, or across batches (e.g. mixing time, drying time, dirty/clean hold, bulk hold, compounding-to-filtration).
config_options: start event and stop event (any step/phase event, equipment status change or material status change)
minimum duration, maximum duration, alert threshold before maximum
scope: within step, across unit procedures, across batches (intermediate hold)
behaviour at maximum: exception only or exception plus block
display of live countdown on operator and supervisor screens
engine_enforced_rules: durations are computed from server timestamps of recorded events, never typed by users
a step guarded by a minimum time cannot complete early
exceeding a maximum always creates an exception; configuration can add blocking but cannot suppress the exception
timers continue independently of client sessions and survive restarts
time-limit values must reference an approved source (validation/hold-time study) in the MBR
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111 (time limits for each production phase; deviations justified and documented); FDA guidance Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing (2004) on time limits; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022)

name: Verification / witness
purpose: Independent check of a performed action or entered value by a second person, either concurrently (witness) or immediately after (verification).
config_options: target step(s) or fields
mode: concurrent witness within a time window, or subsequent verification
verifier role(s)
what the verifier must actively re-check (re-scan container, view scale display, compare values)
optional stricter independence (e.g. not the same shift lead)
engine_enforced_rules: verifier must be a different authenticated individual from the performer
verification cannot precede the verified action and must show the actual evidence (values, scans, images)
signature meaning recorded as verification

mandatory where regulation requires it (manual charge-in, manual yield calculation, critical manual data entry) and cannot be removed; reduced to a single checking person only when qualified automated equipment performed the operation
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(c)-(d), 211.103, 211.68(c), 211.188(b)(11); EU GMP Annex 11 section 6; EU GMP Chapter 4

name: QA hold point / in-process release gate
purpose: Stop the flow until the quality unit reviews evidence and releases (or rejects) an intermediate or the continuation of the batch.
config_options: gate position in the flow
evidence required (IPC results, LIMS results, EM data, open exceptions list)
authorised role and number of signatures
permitted dispositions (release, release with conditions, reject, hold)
engine_enforced_rules: all downstream steps are locked until an authorised QA disposition is signed
a gate cannot be released while a mandatory result is missing or failing without a documented QA decision on the related exception
rejection sets the intermediate status to rejected and blocks its use in any batch
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.22(a) (quality unit authority over in-process materials), 211.110(c), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 1 and Chapter 5

name: Exception / event capture and deviation link
purpose: Record any departure from the MBR or any system-detected breach during execution, and connect it to the QMS deviation process.
config_options: exception categories and default routing
which categories allow the operator to continue vs require supervisor/QA acknowledgement first
mandatory fields per category
QMS integration mapping (create deviation, link existing)
engine_enforced_rules: system-detected breaches (limit, status override, time limit, interface failure, late entry) always create exceptions; they cannot be switched off per MBR
operators can raise an exception at any step
exceptions cannot be deleted, only dispositioned with reason and signature
batch record review/release is blocked while any exception is open
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(b), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 1, Chapter 4 (deviations with signed authorisation); EU GMP Annex 16 (QP takes deviations into account)

name: Sub-procedure / library element call
purpose: Re-use an approved, parameterised sequence (library element, e.g. 'drain vessel', 'screen integrity check', 'PUPSIT') inside an MBR by reference.
config_options: referenced library element and version
parameter bindings for this call
instance name/label
equipment binding for the instance
engine_enforced_rules: the referenced version is frozen when the MBR is approved; execution never silently picks up a newer element version
where-used index is maintained; a new library version triggers impact assessment and, if adopted, new MBR versions
library elements have their own author/checker/approval lifecycle
parameters passed must satisfy the element's declared types, units and ranges at design time
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(a), 211.186; EU GMP Annex 11 section 10 (change and configuration management)

name: Conditional branch
purpose: Choose between alternative paths based on recorded data (e.g. LOD result, equipment type bound, product variant) or an explicit, authorised operator choice.
config_options: condition expressions over recorded data or parameters
branch targets and labels
operator-choice branch with allowed roles and mandatory reason
variant-driven branches resolved at record issuance (e.g. coating type for this product)
engine_enforced_rules: design-time check that conditions are exhaustive, non-overlapping and every branch is reachable
branch taken and its triggering data are recorded; untaken branches are marked not applicable by the system, not by users
variant branches resolved at issuance appear in the issued record as fixed, so reviewers see only the executed path plus the decision
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(f), 211.100(b), 211.186(b)(9); ISA-88 Part 2 PFC alternative branches

name: Loop / repeat-until
purpose: Repeat a sequence until an endpoint is reached (e.g. dry and test LOD until within limit, adjust pH until in range, re-sample coating weight gain) with a bounded number of iterations.
config_options: loop body
exit condition over recorded data
maximum iterations and/or maximum elapsed time
action when maximum reached (exception, QA gate)
engine_enforced_rules: every iteration's data is retained in order; iterations cannot overwrite each other
exceeding the maximum always raises an exception

loops are allowed only on parameters classified as process endpoints in the approved MBR; a loop whose exit condition is a release or acceptance test is rejected at design time (retesting of such results follows the OOS procedure instead of an MBR loop)
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110, 211.192; FDA guidance Investigating OOS Test Results (Rev. 1, May 2022) which covers in-process lab tests and rejects averaging original with retest results

name: Parallel branches and synchronisation
purpose: Allow independent sequences to run concurrently (e.g. binder preparation while dry mixing; component preparation while compounding) and join them before a dependent step.
config_options: branches and their join type (all mandatory branches complete, or first-of)
location/resource constraints per branch
maximum skew allowed between branches (optional time limit)
engine_enforced_rules: a join step cannot start until the required branches are complete
shared equipment or material conflicts between branches are detected and blocked
each branch keeps its own attributable record and timestamps
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(f); ISA-88 Part 2 PFC simultaneous branches

name: Attachment and external evidence capture
purpose: Attach evidence that originates outside the eBR (instrument printouts, cycle reports, photos, supplier certificates) to a step.
config_options: permitted file types
required metadata (instrument ID, cycle/run number, time range)
capture method: electronic import from source system, scan of paper original, photo
reviewer role
engine_enforced_rules: attachments are hashed and immutable once saved; replacement is a new version with reason
where the source system keeps the original electronic data, the record links to or imports it rather than relying on a static PDF
scans of paper originals must be certified as true copies by an authorised person before the paper may be discarded
attachments appear in the review package; unreviewed attachments block review completion
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c); EU GMP Annex 11 sections 7-8; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on true copies and dynamic vs static records

name: Yield and reconciliation
purpose: Compute actual yield vs theoretical at each appropriate stage and reconcile quantities (good output, samples, rejects, waste, retained, returned).
config_options: stage at which yield is computed
theoretical yield basis (formula total, actual charged quantities, or previous stage output)
categories counted in the balance
minimum and maximum percentage of theoretical yield
reconciliation tolerance for unit counts
engine_enforced_rules: an MBR cannot be approved if a configured yield stage lacks min/max limits
yield is computed by the validated engine from recorded quantities, then verified by one person (automated) or independently by a second person (manual)
result outside limits raises an exception that requires investigation before release
sample, waste and reject quantities recorded in other steps flow in automatically, not re-typed
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.103, 211.186(b)(7), 211.188(b), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 5 (yields and reconciliation)

name: Printed packaging material / label issuance and reconciliation
purpose: Issue labels, cartons, leaflets and printed foils/lidding to a packaging batch under strict control and reconcile issued, used, destroyed, returned and damaged quantities.
config_options: items and approved artwork/version per market
issuance quantity rule (batch size plus allowance)
counting method (roll counter, weigh-count, manual count with verification)
reconciliation limits per item (narrow, based on historical data)
disposal rule for batch-coded surplus vs return of uncoded surplus
specimen capture (scanned or photographed printed specimen)
engine_enforced_rules: only released lots of the artwork version specified for this MBR/market can be issued (scan-verified)
the quantity balance must close; a discrepancy outside the preset limits raises an exception requiring investigation
batch-coded surplus must be recorded as destroyed (with witness); it cannot be returned to stock
specimens of all printed labelling used are captured in the record
an MBR cannot be approved with labelling steps lacking reconciliation limits
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.122, 211.125(c) (reconciliation with narrow preset limits based on historical data; investigation per 211.192), 211.130, 211.188(b) (labeling control records incl. specimens); EU GMP Chapter 5 (printed packaging materials)

name: Online variable-data printing and vision/code verification with challenge tests
purpose: Print lot, expiry (and serial) data on packs/labels from the batch record and prove the printing and inspection devices work, via start/periodic/end challenge tests.
config_options: variable data fields mapped from batch record (lot, expiry, manufacturing date, market-specific formats)
printer and camera/code reader device IDs
challenge test plan: triggers (start, after stoppage, periodic, end) and challenge types (wrong code, missing print, unreadable code, reject-bin verification)
first-print approval by second person or QA
engine_enforced_rules: variable data is transferred to the printer from the batch record; no manual keying at the device
printed data is compared to the batch record before running; mismatch blocks
challenge tests are mandatory at configured triggers; a failed or missed challenge stops the line step and raises an exception
device events (rejects, stops, parameter changes) are captured with timestamps
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.122(g) (special controls incl. 100% electronic verification for cut labeling), 211.130, 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 5 (on-line printing checks)

name: Serialisation and aggregation
purpose: Commission serial numbers onto saleable units and aggregate them to higher packaging levels for US DSCSA and EU FMD markets.
config_options: target market profile (US DSCSA product identifier with NDC/serial/lot/expiry; EU FMD unique identifier with GTIN/serial/batch/expiry plus anti-tampering device)
serial number source (Level 4/5 serialisation system)
aggregation hierarchy (unit, bundle, case, pallet)
sample and destroy handling (decommission reasons)
rework rules for re-packing
engine_enforced_rules: serials only from the authorised pool; every serial ends in a defined state (commissioned, decommissioned with reason, destroyed)
serial reconciliation closes before packaging completion
packaging batch cannot be released until serialisation data has been handed to the upstream system (and, for EU, confirmed uploaded to the repository as required by the process design)
anti-tampering device application is verified where the market requires it
regulatory_basis: US Drug Supply Chain Security Act (FD&C Act section 582); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161 (safety features)

name: Output/intermediate container registration and status labelling
purpose: Create uniquely identified containers of intermediate, bulk or finished product with tare/gross/net and quarantine status, and print their labels.
config_options: container types and tare source (weighed vs nominal)
sub-lot/container numbering scheme
label template per material type
initial status (default quarantine) and destination location
engine_enforced_rules: each container gets a system-unique ID and label printed from system data
net = gross - tare computed by the engine; quantities feed yield and inventory
status is quarantine until a QA disposition changes it; quarantined containers can't be consumed by a subsequent step unless the MBR explicitly allows use pending results under QA-approved conditions
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.80(d) (container identification and status), 211.105, 211.110(c); EU GMP Chapter 5 (labelling and status of containers)

name: Intermediate/bulk hold and transfer
purpose: Control storage and transfer of intermediates or bulk between stages or batches with validated hold times and storage conditions.
config_options: maximum hold time per material/stage (reference to hold-time study)
required storage conditions and location types
transfer approvals
re-test requirement if hold approaches limit
engine_enforced_rules: hold clock starts at the recorded completion event and is checked at the time of next use
use after expiry of hold is blocked unless QA dispositions an exception
storage location and condition excursions during the hold are pulled into the record
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111; EU GMP Chapter 5; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) for sterile holds

name: Personnel qualification and training check
purpose: Ensure the person executing, verifying or approving a step is trained/qualified for it at that moment (the injectables edition adds gowning/APS qualification, see separate block).
config_options: training prerequisites per step type, MBR or equipment (curriculum items, SOP versions)
qualification types (e.g. equipment operator licence, visual inspector qualification)
grace rules (none by default)
presence log of persons in the room/line (optional)
engine_enforced_rules: qualification status is evaluated at action time against the training system of record; expired or missing qualification blocks the action
training on the effective MBR/SOP version is required where configured as a prerequisite; a new MBR version can trigger read-and-understand training before use
the qualification evidence (status snapshot) is stored with the action
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.25, 21 CFR 11.10(i); EU GMP Chapter 2

name: Section sign-off (production supervisor review)
purpose: Close a unit procedure/stage with a responsible-person review before the next stage or before QA review.
config_options: which sections require sign-off
reviewer role
checklist for the reviewer (exceptions acknowledged, attachments reviewed)
whether a performer in the section may also sign off
engine_enforced_rules: sign-off is possible only when all steps in the section are complete or system/authorised-NA, and all exceptions in the section are at least acknowledged
signature meaning 'reviewed' with timestamp; the reviewed content is hashed into the signature
a later correction to any step in the section invalidates the sign-off visibly and requires re-sign-off
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Chapter 4 (approval by the person responsible for processing operations); 21 CFR 211.188(b)(11) (persons directly supervising or checking)

name: Batch record review (review by exception) and disposition
purpose: End-of-batch QA review of the executed record focused on exceptions, followed by disposition (US quality unit approval; EU QP certification per Annex 16).
config_options: review stages and roles (production review, QA review, QP certification)
exception categories that must be individually reviewed (the mandatory set cannot be reduced)
audit-trail review scope for critical data (which data classes)
release interface to ERP
engine_enforced_rules: review cannot complete while steps are incomplete, exceptions open, attachments unreviewed, or linked deviations/QC results outstanding
the review-by-exception report is generated by the engine from all exceptions, corrections, late entries, overrides and critical audit-trail events; configuration cannot hide any of these
audit-trail entries for changes to critical data are presented for review before final approval
only users with the quality unit role (US) / QP role (EU) can sign disposition/certification; the person releasing is identified in the record
after disposition the record is locked; post-release corrections follow a controlled amendment process
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.22, 211.192; EU GMP Annex 16; EU GMP Annex 11 section 15 (only QPs certify via the system); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on audit trail review before final approval

name: Material return, waste and destruction record
purpose: Record unused material returned to stores, waste and rejected units, and destruction of materials, feeding reconciliation.
config_options: return reasons and destinations
waste categories
destruction witness requirement
engine_enforced_rules: returned material comes back with quarantine/appropriate status and its own label; quantities feed reconciliation automatically
destruction of batch-coded or rejected materials is witnessed by a second person
quantities cannot be edited after reconciliation without a correction record

name: Reprocessing / rework gate
purpose: Allow a batch or intermediate to be reprocessed only through an approved reprocessing procedure authorised by the quality unit.
config_options: library of approved reprocessing sub-procedures
entry conditions (e.g. linked investigation reference)
additional testing requirements
engine_enforced_rules: a reprocessing path can only be entered with a QA authorisation referencing an investigation/deviation
the reprocessing sub-procedure must itself be an approved master; ad-hoc steps are impossible
genealogy links the reprocessed material to the original batch and the record shows the rework path explicitly
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.115 (reprocessing procedures, quality unit review and approval); EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Packaging line inspection-device challenge (checkweigher, code reader, reject verification)
purpose: Verify at defined times that in-line inspection devices (checkweighers, code/vision readers, missing-leaflet detectors, reject gates) detect and reject defective units.
config_options: device list per line
challenge types and number of challenge pieces
frequency: start, after interruptions, periodic, end
acceptance: all challenge pieces rejected into the verified reject bin
engine_enforced_rules: challenge results recorded per device and time; failure stops the dependent step and raises an exception
output produced since the last successful challenge is flagged for evaluation if a challenge fails
missed scheduled challenges are exceptions at review
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(a) (routine checking of automatic equipment), 211.122(g), 211.130; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Binder/granulating-fluid preparation and wet granulation endpoint
purpose: Prepare the binder solution/granulating liquid and run high-shear or fluid-bed granulation to a defined endpoint.
config_options: binder preparation sub-steps (solvent quantity, dissolution time, temperature, visual clarity check) and its hold time
granulator class (high-shear, fluid-bed)
parameters: impeller/chopper speeds, liquid addition rate and total, spray rate/atomisation pressure (fluid-bed), inlet air temperature/volume
endpoint criterion: time, power consumption/torque, total liquid, or combination
wet massing time
engine_enforced_rules: binder solution must be used within its validated hold time
liquid quantity added is captured from the load cell/flow meter and compared to the approved range
endpoint parameter trace and the endpoint value are recorded from the equipment where interfaced; manual endpoint calls require a reason and verification
any parameter outside its proven acceptable range raises an exception

name: Drying with LOD endpoint loop
purpose: Dry wet granules (fluid-bed or tray) and sample for loss on drying until the moisture endpoint is met.
config_options: dryer class and drying parameters (inlet/outlet/product temperature, airflow, time)
LOD method (moisture analyser, instrument ID class), sample size
LOD limits (upper and, if needed, lower)
maximum drying iterations and total drying time
sampling location(s)
engine_enforced_rules: each LOD iteration is kept with time, sample, instrument and result; later iterations cannot overwrite earlier ones
exit only when the endpoint criterion is met; exceeding the maximum iterations or time raises an exception
over-drying below a lower limit (if configured) is an exception, not silently accepted
moisture analyser calibration/performance check status verified before use

name: Dry granulation (roller compaction / slugging)
purpose: Record and control roller compaction or slugging, including ribbon/slug checks, and subsequent size reduction.
config_options: roll pressure/force, roll gap, roll speed, feed screw speed, vacuum deaeration
ribbon checks: thickness, density/solid fraction, frequency
integrated mill screen size and speed
recycle of fines allowed or not and its limit
engine_enforced_rules: parameters captured from the compactor where interfaced; excursions outside approved ranges create exceptions
periodic ribbon checks are scheduled and missed checks are flagged
recycled fines quantity (if allowed) is recorded and kept within the approved limit

name: Milling/sieving with screen integrity check
purpose: Size-reduce or screen material and prove the screen/sieve was intact before and after use (to exclude metal/mesh contamination).
config_options: mill/sieve class and screen size/type ID
mill speed and feed rate
screen integrity check at start and end (visual, photo)
action on damaged screen (quarantine of material processed since last good check)
engine_enforced_rules: the specific screen ID is scanned and must be of the approved size/type
pre-use and post-use integrity checks are mandatory; a failed post-use check raises an exception and holds the material processed
screen use is logged against the screen's own logbook

name: Blending/lubrication and blend uniformity sampling
purpose: Blend (and lubricate) to the approved endpoint and, where required, sample for blend uniformity (thief sampling or in-line NIR/PAT).
config_options: blender class, fill level range, rotation speed, blending time or number of revolutions, lubrication time
order of addition
blend uniformity plan: number and positions of sampling locations, sample size (1-3x unit dose), replicate samples
PAT option: NIR model reference, endpoint criterion, data import
engine_enforced_rules: blending time/revolutions are measured from equipment or timer, not typed; minimum and maximum enforced
over-lubrication (exceeding maximum lubrication time) raises an exception
blend samples get unique IDs by location and are linked to LIMS; missing locations are flagged
PAT results are stored with model version and status; a model-predicted endpoint does not waive physical sampling unless the approved control strategy says so
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(3) (adequacy of mixing), 211.160; FDA draft guidance on 211.110 (Jan 2025) on process models; FDA's 2003 stratified-sampling draft guidance was withdrawn in 2013

name: Compression set-up with tooling
purpose: Set up the rotary press for a product: bind the press and the punch/die set, verify tooling identity/condition, load approved machine settings and approve first tablets.
config_options: press class and number of stations; single-sided or double-sided (left/right) output
tooling set requirements (shape, dimensions, embossing/debossing, tip type, multi-tip)
tooling checks: set ID scan, visual inspection, punch length measurement tolerance, cumulative compression count vs tooling life limit
machine settings template (turret speed, pre-/main compression force, fill depth, feeder speed) with approved ranges
first-off/start-up checks and number of start-up rejects to discard
engine_enforced_rules: tooling set must match the product's approved tooling specification; wrong embossing/shape blocks start
tooling past its usage/inspection limit or with a failed inspection cannot be bound
settings outside approved ranges require an exception; changes during the run are captured with time and user
first-off tablets must pass the configured start-up IPC before routine compression is released
tooling usage counter is updated from press counts at the end of the run

name: Periodic compression IPC scheduler (multi-station / left-right)
purpose: Schedule and enforce in-process checks during compression at defined intervals, separately per press side/output and for events (start, restart, parameter change, end).
config_options: interval by time (e.g. every 30 min) or by count of tablets/turret revolutions
separate sampling streams per side (left/right) or per layer/output
event triggers: start-up, after stoppage > X min, after setting change, end of run, container change
tests per check (weight, breaking force, thickness, appearance, friability, disintegration) with different frequencies
grace window before a check is overdue
engine_enforced_rules: an overdue check raises an alert, then an exception; tablets produced after a missed check are flagged for evaluation
a failing check puts the output since the last passing check on hold (container-level traceability via container IDs)
samples and results are tied to side/station stream and to the time window they represent
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(1)-(2) (weight variation, disintegration), 211.110(b); EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Tablet weight uniformity IPC with statistics
purpose: Weigh n individual tablets (and/or group weights of 10/20) per check and evaluate against absolute and mean-relative limits.
config_options: n tablets per check; individual and/or group weighing
target mass and limits: mean limits, individual limits absolute or as % deviation from mean in two tiers
statistics: mean, SD, RSD, min, max, count outside tier 1/tier 2
balance interface and auto-print ticket import
control-chart display (mean and range) across the run
engine_enforced_rules: all individual weights captured from the balance; manual entry flagged and verified
tier rules evaluated exactly (e.g. no more than k outside the tier-1 deviation and none outside tier-2) using the computed mean
balance must be calibrated and suitable (minimum weight) for the tablet mass
a failed evaluation places output since the last good check on hold
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(1); Ph. Eur. 2.9.5 uniformity of mass (tiered deviations relative to average mass); USP <905>

name: Tablet physical IPC: breaking force, thickness, diameter
