purpose: Capture multi-parameter measurements per tablet from an automatic tablet tester or manual gauges and evaluate them.
config_options: parameters per tablet (weight, thickness, diameter/length, breaking force) and units (N or kp with conversion)
n tablets per check and per side
limits per parameter (mean and individual)
tester integration (one record per tablet with all parameters)
engine_enforced_rules: multi-parameter readings stay linked per tablet (no re-sorting that breaks the link)
unit conversions only via the UoM service (e.g. kp to N)
tester ID and calibration status stored; manual gauge values need verification
failing results create exceptions and hold output since last good check
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a); USP <1217> (tablet breaking force) as method reference

name: Friability test
purpose: Perform the friability test on a tablet sample and compute percentage weight loss, with the compendial repeat logic.
config_options: sample size rule by unit mass
number of drum revolutions
limit for mean weight loss
repeat rule when the first result is doubtful
observation of broken/cracked tablets as fail criterion
engine_enforced_rules: initial and final masses captured from the balance; % loss computed by the engine
when the configured repeat rule is triggered, all runs are kept and the mean is computed from all of them (no discarding of the first run)
presence of cracked/broken tablets is a mandatory question, not optional
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a); USP <1216> / Ph. Eur. 2.9.7 tablet friability (harmonised)

name: Disintegration test (in-process)
purpose: Run and record the in-process disintegration test for tablets (uncoated, film-coated, enteric with acid stage, orodispersible/effervescent variants).
config_options: apparatus and medium, temperature
number of units and time limit per dosage-form type
enteric variant: acid stage duration and requirement, then buffer stage
retest rule per compendium
engine_enforced_rules: bath temperature and instrument status checked before start
per-unit results recorded; the compendial retest rule is applied exactly and all results retained
time is measured by the engine or instrument, not typed
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(2); USP <701> / Ph. Eur. 2.9.1 disintegration

name: Bilayer / multilayer compression checks
purpose: Control multilayer tablets where each layer has its own blend, fill and weight, plus layer-sequence and interface integrity checks.
config_options: layers, blends per layer and layer order
first-layer tamping force and final compression force
layer weight checks (e.g. first-layer-only samples by press sampling mode) and total weight checks
layer-specific IPC frequencies
layer separation/delamination check
engine_enforced_rules: each layer's feed is bound to the correct blend container (scan); swapping blends between hoppers is blocked
layer weights and total weight are evaluated separately against their own limits
layer-only samples are identified as such and never mixed with full-tablet statistics

name: Press automatic weight control and reject system verification
purpose: Record the press's force-based automatic weight control settings, reject counts and reject-gate challenge results; import press event data.
config_options: force-weight control mode and limits (individual reject limits, mean control limits)
start-up reject quantity
reject-gate challenge frequency and method
press data to import (force trends, rejects, stops, speed)
engine_enforced_rules: control limits downloaded from approved values and read back
reject counts imported into reconciliation; rejected tablets cannot be returned to the good stream
reject-gate challenge failures hold output since the last good challenge
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(a)-(b), 211.110(a); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5

name: Metal detection and deduster challenge
purpose: Pass tablets through deduster and metal detector and verify detection capability with certified test pieces at defined times.
config_options: test piece types and sizes (ferrous, non-ferrous, stainless)
challenge timing (start, periodic, after stop, end)
reject handling and inspection of rejected tablets
engine_enforced_rules: test piece IDs are scanned and must be within certification
a failed challenge holds tablets processed since the last passing challenge and raises an exception
metal detector reject counts feed reconciliation
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(a), 211.110; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Coating suspension/solution preparation and hold
purpose: Prepare the film/sugar/functional coating dispersion and control its solids content, mixing and hold time.
config_options: coating system material(s) and solvent (aqueous vs organic with solvent safety checks)
target solids % and quantity (theoretical plus spray loss allowance)
mixing time and speed, de-aeration, sieving
maximum hold time and required continuous stirring
engine_enforced_rules: quantities computed and verified as for any formula calculation
hold time from preparation end to end of use enforced; expired dispersion cannot be used without QA disposition
continuous stirring confirmation (from equipment or periodic check) where configured

name: Coating process and weight gain
purpose: Run pan (or fluid-bed) coating, capture process parameters and determine coating weight gain to the endpoint; for functional coats, link to functional IPC (e.g. acid resistance).
config_options: pan load range (kg of cores) and pan speed
inlet/exhaust/product temperature, airflow, spray rate, atomising and pattern air pressures
weight gain determination: sample of n cores tared before coating vs coated weight, or total batch mass; target and limits
endpoint: theoretical dispersion sprayed, weight gain reached, or both
functional coat IPC reference (e.g. acid stage disintegration/dissolution) and polishing/curing step
engine_enforced_rules: weight gain computed by the engine from recorded core and coated masses at full precision
endpoint cannot be declared before the minimum weight gain or dispersion quantity is reached; exceeding maxima raises exceptions
parameters from the coater are imported with timestamps; manual readings flagged

name: Imprinting / laser marking verification
purpose: Verify tablet imprint or laser marking content and legibility during printing.
config_options: marking content from the approved product specification
check frequency and sample size
defect categories (smudged, missing, misregistered)
vision system integration
engine_enforced_rules: marking content is derived from product master data, not typed at the line
defect counts roll into reconciliation and AQL where configured
failed checks hold output since last good check
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110, 211.130; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Blister packaging set-up and sealing control
purpose: Set up a thermoform or cold-form blister line for a pack format and control forming/sealing parameters and foil/film identity.
config_options: pack format (cavities per blister, blisters per carton) and change-part set ID
forming/lidding materials (PVC, PVC/PVDC, Alu-Alu cold form, lidding foil with print) with item codes
forming temperature, sealing temperature, pressure, dwell/speed ranges
feeder and empty-pocket detection settings
sample blisters for appearance and print check
engine_enforced_rules: change parts and materials are scanned and must match the pack format of the MBR; printed lidding follows label-issuance rules
sealing parameters downloaded/read back or captured; excursions outside validated ranges create exceptions and hold affected output
empty/broken-pocket rejects are counted into reconciliation
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.122, 211.130, 211.186(b)(6) (packaging materials in master record), 211.68

name: Blister/strip leak test
purpose: Periodic seal-integrity test of blisters/strips (e.g. dye ingress under vacuum or vacuum decay) as an in-process control.
config_options: method (dye ingress, vacuum decay) and instrument class
vacuum level, hold time and sample size (blisters/strips, per track)
frequency (start, periodic, after stops, after reel change, end)
pass/fail per cavity and action on failure
engine_enforced_rules: test parameters actually applied (vacuum, time) are captured from the tester or verified by a second person
any leaking cavity fails the check, holds output since the last passing check and raises an exception
missed scheduled tests are exceptions at review
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110, 211.130, 211.94 (container closure protection); USP <1207> principles as method guidance

name: Bottle packaging: count, desiccant, closure torque and induction seal
purpose: Control bottle filling of tablets: count verification, desiccant/filler insertion, cap application torque and induction seal integrity.
config_options: count per bottle and counter type (electronic/slat)
desiccant/cotton insertion and verification method
cap torque target and limits (application and removal)
induction seal check method and frequency
reject verification of the counter and cap/seal detectors
engine_enforced_rules: count verification checks are scheduled; failures hold output since last good check
torque readings captured from the torque tester with its calibration status
missing desiccant/seal detections are rejected and counted; detector challenge failures stop the step

name: Aseptic personnel qualification and gowning check
purpose: Gate entry to and work in Grade A/B aseptic operations on current gowning qualification, aseptic-behaviour training and successful APS participation.
config_options: qualification types required per room grade/operation (gowning qualification, aseptic technique, intervention-specific training, APS participation)
requalification intervals from the site CCS (e.g. annual gowning reassessment, APS participation within the defined period)
integration with access control/training system
visual gowning check at entry (checklist) and post-session glove/gown monitoring link
engine_enforced_rules: a person without current gowning qualification and APS participation cannot be recorded as performing or intervening in Grade A/B aseptic steps
qualification status snapshot is stored with each aseptic action
personnel monitoring results (glove/gown prints) are linked to the person and session and flow into EM review for the batch
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 7 (personnel: gowning qualification, reassessment at least annually, unsupervised Grade A/B access only after gowning assessment and successful APS); 21 CFR 211.25, 211.28; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Environmental and personnel monitoring linkage
purpose: Link the batch to viable and non-viable monitoring of its processing sessions (settle plates, active air, contact plates, glove prints, continuous particle counts) so results are part of batch review.
config_options: EM plan per room/line and session (locations, sample types, frequencies) referenced from the EM system
session boundaries (start/end of filling, interventions)
alert/action levels by grade (from EM system)
which results are required before batch disposition (incubated plate reads)
engine_enforced_rules: EM samples for each session are created/linked automatically when the session starts; missing samples are exceptions
Grade A continuous particle monitoring data for the session window is imported and excursions become exceptions
batch disposition is blocked until all linked EM results (including incubated plates) are available and excursions dispositioned
EM trend data for the period is presented in the batch review package
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 9 (EM; continuous Grade A particle monitoring; EM trend data reviewed as part of batch certification/release); 21 CFR 211.42(c)(10)(iv), 211.113(b); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Compounding with WFI and pH/volume adjustment
purpose: Prepare the bulk solution/suspension: WFI addition, dissolution of components, pH adjustment loop, make-up to final weight/volume, in-process checks.
config_options: WFI use point, required WFI temperature/quality release status
order and rate of additions, mixing speed/time, temperature, nitrogen sparging/blanketing
pH target and limits, adjusting agents and maximum cumulative additions
final make-up basis (weight with density, or volume)
IPC: pH, density, appearance/clarity, assay/osmolality via LIMS
start of compounding-to-filtration time-limit clock
engine_enforced_rules: WFI loop/use point status must be released (no active excursion) at time of draw
each pH adjustment iteration is recorded; exceeding the maximum adjusting agent quantity raises an exception
final quantity computed and checked by the engine (weight/density/volume conversions)
compounding start event automatically starts the chained time limits to filtration and filling
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101, 211.110(a)(5)-(6) (solution clarity/completeness/pH; bioburden), 211.111; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) time limits

name: Pre-filtration bioburden sampling
purpose: Sample the bulk immediately before sterilising filtration for bioburden (and endotoxin where required), with results linked to disposition.
config_options: sample volume, point and timing relative to filtration start
limit (from filter validation/registration)
LIMS test mapping
engine_enforced_rules: filtration cannot start before the bioburden sample is recorded
result is linked to the batch; disposition blocked until available; a result above limit raises an exception
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(6), 211.113(b); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (bioburden before sterilisation/filtration); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Sterilising filtration with filter integrity testing (PUPSIT and post-use)
purpose: Execute sterilising-grade filtration and prove filter integrity before use (after sterilisation) and after use, with integrity-tester data captured.
config_options: filter/assembly type and validated filter part numbers
integrity test method (bubble point, diffusion/forward flow, pressure hold, water intrusion) and product-/wetting-fluid-specific limits
PUPSIT required, or not applicable with reference to an approved risk assessment
redundant filter configuration and which filter is tested
filtration parameters: max differential pressure, flow, max filtration time, max volume/throughput
engine_enforced_rules: filter and housing IDs scanned; part number must match validated list; filter must be within sterilisation hold time
pre-use (post-sterilisation) integrity test must pass before product filtration starts unless the MBR carries a QA-approved PUPSIT justification
post-use non-destructive integrity test is mandatory before the filter is removed from its housing; a failure raises a critical exception and blocks disposition
integrity test results imported from the tester with instrument ID, test parameters and raw values; manual transcription only as flagged fallback with verification
filtration time and differential pressure limits enforced
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) section 8.87 (PUPSIT; post-use integrity test); 21 CFR 211.113(b); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) on filtration efficacy and integrity testing

name: Sterilisation cycle record (autoclave / SIP) for equipment and components
purpose: Record each sterilisation run of equipment, change parts, filters, stoppers or garments: load, validated cycle, cycle data, indicators, and resulting sterile-hold expiry.
config_options: steriliser class and validated cycle IDs allowed per load type
load pattern reference (validated loading configuration) and item list per load
cycle parameters to capture (temperature, pressure, time at temperature, F0, drying) and acceptance limits
biological/chemical indicator use and result capture
sterile hold time per item type and wrapping/protection method
engine_enforced_rules: only validated cycle IDs for the declared load pattern can be selected
cycle data imported from the steriliser controller/SCADA with cycle number; the cycle report is attached; a failed or aborted cycle cannot yield 'sterile' status
items get a sterile status with a sterile-hold expiry computed by the engine; expired or unsterile items are blocked from use in aseptic steps
sterilisation records are presented for review as part of batch disposition
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (sterilisation: records per run reviewed for batch release; BIs unless parametric release authorised; defined storage time for sterilised items); 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.67; FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) time limits for sterilised equipment/containers/closures

name: Depyrogenation (dry-heat tunnel or oven)
purpose: Depyrogenate and sterilise glass containers (vials, ampoules, cartridges) or other heat-stable items, capturing the validated time-temperature profile.
config_options: tunnel/oven class and validated programme per container format
belt speed, hot-zone temperature, cooling-zone parameters and differential pressures
acceptance limits and data capture interval
hold time of depyrogenated containers before filling
engine_enforced_rules: only the validated programme for the container format can be used; format mismatch blocks
temperature/belt-speed/pressure excursions during the run raise exceptions and identify affected containers/time window
depyrogenated containers inherit an expiry; filling with expired containers is blocked
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (dry heat sterilisation/depyrogenation); Ph. Eur. 5.1.2/2.6.8 context; 21 CFR 211.94(c), 211.113(b)

name: Primary component preparation and RTU/nested component acceptance
purpose: Prepare stoppers, seals and containers (washing, siliconisation, sterilisation) or accept ready-to-use (RTU) sterile nested tubs/bags for vials, cartridges and prefilled syringes, including transfer decontamination into Grade A.
config_options: component type and preparation route (in-house wash/sterilise vs RTU)
RTU acceptance checks: supplier sterilisation certificate/lot release, bag/tub integrity, expiry
transfer method into the isolator/RABS (e-beam tunnel, VHP pass-box, decontaminated bag port) and its cycle record
count/quantity per tub and reconciliation
engine_enforced_rules: RTU lots must be released by QA and within expiry; integrity check of outer packaging recorded before transfer
transfer decontamination cycle must be completed and passed before components enter Grade A
component quantities feed reconciliation of filled units
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapters 5 and 8 (transfer of materials into Grade A, sterilisation of components); 21 CFR 211.84, 211.94, 211.113(b)

name: Isolator/RABS decontamination and glove integrity
purpose: Record bio-decontamination cycles (e.g. VHP) of isolators/RABS and glove/sleeve integrity testing around each batch.
config_options: validated decontamination cycle IDs per enclosure
cycle parameters and indicators (chemical/biological) captured
glove integrity test method (physical leak test, visual check) and frequency (at least start and end of batch/campaign; visual checks per session)
action on failed glove test (impact assessment on units filled since last pass)
engine_enforced_rules: aseptic filling cannot start in an enclosure without a passed decontamination cycle within its validity
glove integrity tests are scheduled at the configured points; a failed or missed test raises an exception and flags units filled since the last passing test
glove/port IDs recorded with results
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 4 (glove integrity testing at least at the beginning and end of each batch or campaign; decontamination of isolators); 21 CFR 211.113(b)

name: Sterile process time-limit chain
purpose: Enforce the chained, validated time limits of sterile manufacture across unit procedures (compounding start to filtration end, filtration to filling end, sterile hold of equipment/components, product exposure on line, fill to lyophilisation/stoppering, fill to terminal sterilisation).
config_options: time-limit definitions (start event, stop event, maximum, alert) linked to CCS/validation references
which limits block downstream steps vs raise exception only
display of all running clocks for the batch on a single supervisor view
engine_enforced_rules: all clocks run on server time from recorded events; users cannot enter elapsed times
any exceeded maximum raises an exception; configured blocking limits prevent the next step until QA disposition
time-limit values must cite the supporting validation/hold study in the MBR before approval
all clock results appear in the review-by-exception report
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111; FDA Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing guidance (2004) (time limits incl. compounding to sterilisation, filtration, exposure on line, storage of sterilised items); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8

name: Aseptic filling set-up and fill weight/volume control
purpose: Set up the filling line (format parts, pumps/needles) aseptically and control fill quantity by periodic or 100% in-process weighing, per filling needle.
config_options: container format (vial, ampoule, cartridge, syringe) and format parts IDs
filling system (piston, peristaltic, time-pressure) and number of needles
target fill (weight via density, or volume) with limits per unit and mean; extractable-volume basis
check frequency per needle (start, periodic, after adjustment, end) or 100% in-line checkweighing
adjustment rules and who may adjust
first-units discard quantity at start/restart
engine_enforced_rules: fill weights captured from the (IPC) balance or line checkweigher per needle with timestamps; manual entry flagged and verified
out-of-limit fill triggers exception and reject/hold of units since the last passing check for that needle
every fill adjustment is recorded with before/after values, user and time
units rejected for fill feed reconciliation automatically
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a), 211.113(b); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8; USP <697>/<1151> (container content/extractable volume) as method context

name: Aseptic interventions log
purpose: Record every inherent and corrective intervention in Grade A during aseptic processing, checked against the list of interventions qualified by APS.
config_options: site list of approved interventions (inherent vs corrective) with the APS that qualified each
required details per intervention (who, when, duration, location, units removed, line clearance of affected units)
automatic capture from line events (door open, line stop) where interfaced
classification rules for unplanned interventions
engine_enforced_rules: an intervention not on the APS-qualified list is flagged as an unplanned intervention and raises an exception requiring QA assessment
the performer must hold current qualification for that intervention
line-event data (e.g. RABS door openings) without a matching recorded intervention become exceptions
units to be removed after an intervention are recorded and reconciled
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.16-8.18 (list of interventions evaluated by QRM and APS; recorded in batch documentation) and 9.34 (APS covers inherent and corrective interventions); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004)

name: Stoppering, capping/crimping with missing-stopper rejection
purpose: Control stopper placement and cap/crimp application, rejecting containers with missing or displaced stoppers before capping and checking seal quality.
config_options: stopper height/presence sensor settings (qualified) and challenge frequency
capping location type (Grade A air supply, isolator) and technology
crimp quality checks (visual, residual seal force if used) and frequency
reject verification challenges
engine_enforced_rules: missing/raised-stopper detection must be active and its challenge passed before capping starts; failed challenge stops the step
rejected containers are counted and cannot re-enter the good stream
crimp checks are scheduled; failures hold output since last good check
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (containers with missing or displaced stoppers rejected before capping; capping under Grade A air supply); 21 CFR 211.94

name: Lyophilisation cycle (loading, cycle record, stoppering, unloading)
purpose: Record transfer and loading of partially stoppered containers, the validated freeze-drying cycle, in-chamber stoppering and unloading.
config_options: lyophiliser class and validated cycle recipe IDs per product/fill
loading method (automatic loading system, transfer carts under Grade A) and documented loading pattern
cycle phases and parameters (freezing, primary/secondary drying shelf temperature, chamber pressure, durations), endpoint tests (pressure rise, comparative pressure)
stoppering pressure/gas (nitrogen backfill), chamber sterilisation before load where required
maximum time from filling to start of cycle
engine_enforced_rules: the cycle recipe downloaded is the validated one for the product and read back; recipe edits at the controller are captured and raised as exceptions
transfer and loading steps record Grade A conditions/equipment; loading pattern captured
full cycle trend and alarm list are imported; alarms configured as critical block disposition until assessed
lyophiliser sterilisation status before load is checked where the design requires it (e.g. manual loading without barrier separation)
time limit from filling to cycle start enforced
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.122-8.126 (lyophilisation: transfer of partially closed containers under Grade A, loading pattern documented, sterilisation of manually loaded lyophilisers); 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.111

name: Terminal sterilisation of filled product
purpose: Sterilise sealed containers (typically moist heat) using a validated load and cycle, and record cycle data, indicators and load segregation.
config_options: validated cycle and load pattern per product/container
parameters and limits (temperature, time, F0, pressure/air-over-pressure)
BI/CI placement and results, or parametric release profile where authorised
segregation of sterilised vs non-sterilised loads (status/scan)
maximum time from filling to sterilisation
engine_enforced_rules: only validated cycle/load combinations can be used; cycle data imported and evaluated against limits
a load cannot be marked sterilised without a passing cycle record (and BI results unless parametric release is authorised)
scanning prevents non-sterilised trays from entering the sterilised area/status
fill-to-sterilisation time limit enforced
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (terminal sterilisation, BIs unless parametric release authorised); EU GMP Annex 17 (real-time release/parametric release); 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.167(a)

name: 100% visual inspection and post-inspection AQL
purpose: Record 100% inspection of filled units (manual, semi-automated or automated) with defect classification and counts, followed by acceptance sampling (AQL) of the accepted units.
config_options: inspection mode per product/container (manual booth, semi-automated, automated with validated recipe)
defect library and classes (critical/major/minor; particles, cosmetic, container, closure, fill)
inspector qualification requirements and maximum continuous inspection period before a break
automated inspection recipe ID and challenge (known-defect set) at start/end
AQL sampling plan and acceptance numbers per defect class
reject rate alert/action limits (trend-based) triggering investigation
engine_enforced_rules: only inspectors with current qualification (incl. eyesight check) can record manual inspection; session duration is tracked against the break rule
automated machine must use the validated recipe and pass the challenge set; recipe change during run is an exception
defect counts by class feed reconciliation: inspected = accepted + rejected by class (+ samples)
AQL failure blocks disposition and triggers exception (re-inspection only via approved procedure)
reject rates above limits raise exceptions for investigation
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.30-8.33 (100% inspection; inspector qualification, eyesight checks, breaks; automated inspection validated to be at least as good as manual; defects recorded and trended); USP <790>/<1790> (100% inspection followed by acceptance sampling, AQL 0.65% for visible particles); 21 CFR 211.110, 211.192

name: Container closure integrity testing (in-process)
purpose: Test seal integrity of filled containers: 100% for fusion-sealed small containers (ampoules, BFS) and by sampling for other container types, using validated (preferably deterministic) methods.
config_options: container type and whether 100% testing is mandatory (fusion-sealed, small volume) or sampling (with justified plan)
method (HVLD, vacuum decay, laser headspace, pressure decay; dye ingress only where justified)
instrument/recipe ID and challenge with positive controls
sampling frequency and sample size where not 100%
engine_enforced_rules: for fusion-sealed small-volume containers the MBR cannot be approved without a 100% integrity test step
visual inspection cannot be configured as the integrity test method
test results and rejects imported from the tester with recipe and challenge results; failed challenge holds output since last good challenge
rejected units counted into reconciliation
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.22-8.25 (100% integrity testing of fusion-sealed containers such as ampoules/BFS/small containers; visual inspection not an acceptable integrity method); USP <1207>; 21 CFR 211.94

name: Aseptic process simulation (media fill) execution and reconciliation
purpose: Run an APS as a special batch type from a dedicated MBR variant: growth medium replaces product, worst-case conditions and planned interventions are executed, and every unit is reconciled through incubation and reading.
config_options: APS MBR variant linked to the commercial process it qualifies (line, container, shift, maximum duration, maximum number of personnel)
planned worst-case interventions list and schedule
medium, fill volume, container orientation/inversion, incubation temperatures and durations
personnel participating (for their qualification records)
growth promotion test link
engine_enforced_rules: APS records are clearly typed as APS and can never be released as product
every filled unit is accounted for: filled = incubated + justified discards (e.g. integrity failures) with reasons; unexplained differences are exceptions
any contaminated unit marks the APS failed and triggers investigation; results update line and personnel qualification status automatically
planned interventions not performed, or unplanned ones performed, are highlighted
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 9.32-9.49 (APS design, interventions, incubation and reconciliation of all units, zero-growth target; personnel qualification); FDA aseptic processing guidance (2004) media fill section; 21 CFR 211.113(b)

name: Sterility and endotoxin sampling linked to fill events
purpose: Take finished-product sterility (and endotoxin) samples that represent the batch, including beginning, end and after significant interventions, and link them to LIMS.
config_options: sampling points (start, end, after specific interventions or line stops, per lyophiliser/steriliser load)
number of units per point from the pharmacopoeial/registered sampling plan
LIMS test mapping and result dependencies for disposition
engine_enforced_rules: event-driven samples (e.g. after a corrective intervention) are requested automatically when the event is recorded
sample units are removed from the good count and appear in reconciliation
disposition is blocked until sterility/endotoxin results are received (unless an authorised parametric release applies to sterility)
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.167(a), 211.165; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 10 (sterility test samples representative incl. after interventions); Ph. Eur. 2.6.1 / USP <71>

name: Filled-unit reconciliation across filling, lyophilisation, inspection and CCI
purpose: Reconcile containers from component issue through filling, closing, lyophilisation/sterilisation, visual inspection, CCI and sampling, per stage and overall.
config_options: stages and the unit categories counted at each (issued containers, filled, fill rejects, intervention removals, stoppering/capping rejects, lyo/sterilisation losses, inspection rejects by class, CCI rejects, samples, accepted)
reconciliation tolerance per stage
source of counts (machine counters vs manual counts with verification)
engine_enforced_rules: counts from machines are imported, not typed; manual counts need verification
each stage balance must close within tolerance; unexplained differences raise exceptions blocking disposition
reject categories cannot be merged after the fact; each rejected unit class is traceable to its source step
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.103, 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 5 (reconciliation); EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) (interventions, inspection rejects recorded)

name: Process gas filtration, nitrogen overlay and headspace oxygen
purpose: Control sterile process gases (nitrogen/air for overlay, purging, pressurisation) through sterilising gas filters and verify headspace oxygen for oxygen-sensitive products.
config_options: gas filter IDs and integrity test requirement (pre/post use per CCS)
overlay/purge parameters
headspace oxygen method (laser headspace), limit, frequency
engine_enforced_rules: gas filter integrity status is checked before the gas point is used in Grade A
headspace oxygen results out of limit raise exceptions and hold units since last passing check
gas supply quality release status verified
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 6 (gases in contact with product filtered through sterilising-grade filters; integrity) and chapter 8; 21 CFR 211.113(b)

name: Single-use assembly installation and integrity
purpose: Install pre-sterilised single-use assemblies (bags, tubing, filters, connectors) for compounding, filtration and filling, verifying identity, sterility status and integrity.
config_options: validated assembly part numbers per process step
checks: supplier release/irradiation certificate, expiry, outer packaging integrity, connection method (aseptic connectors, tube welding) and weld inspection
leak/integrity test of the installed assembly where specified
engine_enforced_rules: assembly lot must be released and unexpired; part number must match the MBR
every aseptic connection/weld is recorded with performer and result
assembly integrity failures raise exceptions before product contact
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8 (single-use systems: integrity, supplier qualification, sterility assurance); 21 CFR 211.65, 211.67, 211.84

name: Prefilled syringe/cartridge closure placement
purpose: Control plunger-stopper placement (vacuum or vent-tube) and nest/tub handling for prefilled syringes and cartridges, with positional and functional checks.
config_options: placement method and parameters (vacuum level, insertion depth)
stopper position measurement (camera or gauge) and limits
optional functional IPC (break-loose/glide force) by sampling
tub/nest handling and de-lidding in Grade A
engine_enforced_rules: stopper position results captured from the inspection device; out-of-limit units rejected and counted
placement parameter excursions raise exceptions and identify affected tubs
tub/nest IDs traced from RTU acceptance to filled output
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.94, 211.110; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapter 8

name: Ampoule fusion sealing control
purpose: Control flame/fusion sealing parameters of glass ampoules and link to the mandatory 100% integrity test.
config_options: gas/oxygen flow settings and ranges, sealing station speed
seal appearance checks (tips, bubbles, charring) frequency
link to the downstream 100% CCI step
engine_enforced_rules: sealing parameters captured; excursions flag the affected time window
a batch of ampoules cannot be dispositioned without the 100% integrity test results
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) section 8.22 (fusion-sealed containers subject to 100% integrity testing; seal parameters controlled and monitored)

name: Batch record issuance / order start
purpose: Create the executed batch record (ISA-88 control recipe) from an effective MBR for a specific batch: batch number, batch size, planned equipment, market/variant parameter set.
config_options: batch numbering scheme
allowed batch sizes/range and variant parameter set selection
planned start date and site/line
pre-issuance checks (material availability, equipment availability)
issuance approval (e.g. production planner plus QA for first batch after a change)
engine_enforced_rules: only an Effective MBR version valid for the site/product/batch size can be instantiated; its content hash is stored in the record
batch number is unique system-wide and cannot be reused, even for voided records
voiding a started record requires QA approval and the voided record is retained and linked to its replacement
scaled quantities are computed at issuance and displayed with the calculation trace
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.186, 211.188(a); EU GMP Chapter 4 (batch processing record based on current approved instructions; method avoids transcription errors); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) on control of blank forms/records

name: Equipment cleaning execution record
purpose: Execute and record cleaning of equipment/rooms (between batches, product changeover, campaign end) as a procedure linked to equipment status and logbooks.
config_options: cleaning procedure per equipment class and cleaning type (minor/major, product-specific)
cleaning agents, concentrations, temperatures, times; CIP cycle import
visual inspection checklist and verification
sampling for residues/micro (swab/rinse) with LIMS link
clean-hold time to assign
engine_enforced_rules: completion sets equipment to 'clean' with a clean-hold expiry only after verification and required results
campaign length and dirty-hold limits are enforced from recorded use events
cleaning records are linked into the equipment logbook and to the batches that follow
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.67, 211.182; EU GMP Chapter 3 and Chapter 5; EU GMP Annex 15 (cleaning validation)

rule: Batch disposition is blocked while any step is incomplete, any exception or linked deviation is open, required QC/EM results are missing, or required reviews are unsigned. Only users holding the quality-unit disposition role (US) or the Qualified Person role (EU certification) can sign it; the system records who certified/released, and nobody else (including administrators) can set a released status.
why: The quality unit must review and approve production records and investigate discrepancies before release; Annex 11 requires that when a system records certification and release, only QPs can certify and the releasing person is identified; Annex 16 requires the QP to take deviations into account.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.22, 211.165, 211.192; EU GMP Annex 11 section 15; EU GMP Annex 16

rule: Record completeness is enforced: every step of the issued record ends as executed, system-marked not applicable (untaken branch), or not-applicable by an authorised user with reason and signature. Blank or silently skipped steps are impossible at review.
why: Batch records must include complete information about each significant step; blanks are a classic ambiguity and data integrity finding.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.188(b); EU GMP Chapter 4 (batch processing records); FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: GMP records, audit trails and signatures cannot be deleted by any user or configuration during their retention period; retention periods are floors derived from regulation (e.g. US: at least 1 year after batch expiry, longer for certain OTC products; EU: at least 1 year after expiry or 5 years after QP certification, whichever is longer) and legal holds; archived records stay readable (including metadata and audit trail) for the whole period, across system upgrades.
why: Records must be retained and readily retrievable; archiving must preserve accessibility, readability and integrity.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.180(a); 21 CFR 11.10(c); EU GMP Chapter 4 (retention of batch documentation); EU GMP Annex 11 sections 7 and 17

rule: The system can always produce accurate and complete copies of any batch record in human-readable and electronic form, including all values, corrections, exceptions, signatures with their manifestations, attachments and the audit trail, for inspection; export content cannot be trimmed by report configuration below that minimum.
why: Inspectors must be able to review and copy records; printouts must be clear and indicate changed data.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(b); EU GMP Annex 11 section 8

rule: Configuration layers are separated: MBR/library authors can only compose vendor-defined block types and set their declared options; they cannot alter the engine's enforcement logic. System-level configuration (roles, signature policies, interfaces, rounding policy defaults, numbering) is itself versioned, audit-trailed and changed only via change control, with an exportable, diffable configuration baseline per site/environment.
why: Changes to master records and to the computerised system must be controlled, authorised and documented; configuration drift between validated baseline and production is otherwise undetectable.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 211.100(a); EU GMP Annex 11 sections 4 and 10; GAMP 5 2nd ed. configuration management

rule: Customer-defined calculations run only in a sandboxed, deterministic expression language with a closed library of validated functions, compile-time type and unit checking, no loops without bounds, no I/O, no access to other records except declared inputs, and no ability to write data; there is no 'custom script' escape hatch in GMP masters.
why: Formulas embedded in master records must give correct results; an unrestricted scripting facility would turn every MBR into custom (Category 5) software needing code-level verification and would allow logic that bypasses guardrails.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(b); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) (MPCR calculations validated); GAMP 5 2nd ed. categories

rule: Critical data entered manually always receives an additional accuracy check (second-person verification, double-blind re-entry, or capture from a validated device instead of typing); the MBR author can choose the method but cannot configure 'no check' for data classed as critical (quantities of materials, CPP values, IPC results, yields).
why: Annex 11 requires an additional accuracy check for critical manually entered data, by a second operator or validated electronic means.
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 11 section 6; 21 CFR 211.101(c), 211.103

rule: MBR approval is blocked by automated completeness/plausibility checks that encode regulatory content minima: e.g. theoretical yield with min/max limits at each yield stage, reconciliation limits for printed labelling, limits on every IPC/CPP field, unit of measure on every quantity, time-limit values with a cited validation reference, required verifications on manual charge-in, and (injectables) PUPSIT/post-use integrity and 100% CCI where applicable unless a QA-approved justification is referenced.
why: The master record has mandatory content; catching omissions statically before approval is cheaper and more reliable than relying on reviewers (PAS-X runs 50+ such checks).
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.186(b), 211.125(c), 211.111; EU GMP Chapter 4; EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) sections 8.22 and 8.87

rule: Test, simulation and training executions are technically segregated from GMP execution: they run only on masters in Draft/Test status or in a non-production mode, their records are watermarked, excluded from inventory/equipment/genealogy updates in production, and can never be converted into or merged with GMP batch records; conversely a GMP record can only come from an Effective master.
why: MBR verification by test runs is essential, but test data leaking into GMP records (or unapproved masters producing GMP records) would break record integrity.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(a), 211.186; EU GMP Annex 11 sections 4 and 10; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: The review-by-exception report is generated by the engine from a mandatory exception taxonomy (limit breaches, overrides, corrections, late entries, interface fallbacks, time-limit breaches, open verifications, unplanned interventions, alarm events classed critical, audit-trail events on critical data). Customers may add exception types or raise severities but cannot remove mandatory types or hide events from review.
why: Review by exception is only acceptable if the system provably surfaces everything a full review would find; audit trails of critical data must be reviewed before the record is approved.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.192; EU GMP Annex 11 section 9 (audit trail review) and draft (2025) section 12; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: System administrators (IT/configuration roles) cannot execute, verify, review or release GMP steps, cannot change GMP data values, and cannot grant themselves GMP roles without a second approver; all privileged actions are audit-trailed. Password/lockout/session-timeout policies have regulatory floors that configuration can tighten but not loosen.
why: Segregation of duties and access controls prevent undetected manipulation; Annex 11 expects access restricted to authorised persons and changes to access recorded; Part 11 requires controls over ID codes/passwords.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), 11.300; EU GMP Annex 11 section 12; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018) (restricting admin rights)

rule: Data acquired from instruments, scales, PLC/DCS, BMS/EMS or LIMS keep their provenance (source, device ID, source timestamp, raw value, unit) and the interface verifies completeness/accuracy of transfer; when an interface is bypassed, the value is marked as manually transcribed and requires verification.
why: Electronic data exchange with other systems must include built-in checks for correct and secure entry; input/output of computer systems must be checked for accuracy.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68(b); EU GMP Annex 11 section 5

rule: Every executed step stores the effective versions and actual values of all master data it used (specification limits, equipment status, material status, MBR/library version, SOP version, calculation version). Later master data changes never alter what an executed record shows or how its results were evaluated.
why: Records must reflect what was actually done under the instructions and limits in force at the time; retroactive changes through master data would silently rewrite history.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.188, 11.10(e); EU GMP Chapter 4; EU GMP Annex 11 section 10

rule: If offline or edge execution is supported, offline entries are signed and hashed locally with a trusted, synchronised clock, uploaded in order, never overwrite server data on conflict (conflicts become exceptions), and are flagged as offline-captured for review; signature rules and status checks that need server data are either pre-cached with validity windows or block the step.
why: Network outages must not create gaps in attributability, contemporaneity or sequence enforcement.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.10(e)-(f); EU GMP Annex 11 sections 5, 9 and 16 (business continuity)

rule: Stored values are language- and locale-neutral (canonical number, unit code, UTC time); language, decimal separators and date formats affect display only. Translations of MBR text are approved as part of the MBR version and a language switch can never change a limit, unit or instruction meaning.
why: Multi-language sites must not create divergent instructions or mis-parsed numbers (decimal comma vs point) in the GMP record.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.100(a), 211.186; EU GMP Chapter 4 (clear, unambiguous documents)

rule: The electronic record is the master; any printout is marked as a copy with print time, printer user and record status, and wet-ink signatures on printouts never substitute for the electronic signatures required by the MBR. Hybrid (paper) steps are allowed only as MBR-defined, controlled forms that are issued, reconciled and scanned back as certified true copies.
why: Hybrid situations are a frequent source of ambiguity about which record is authoritative; FDA and the Annex 11 draft address hybrid records and true copies explicitly.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 11.70; EU GMP Annex 11 section 8 and draft (2025) section 13 on hybrid solutions; FDA Data Integrity Q&A (2018)

rule: (Injectables edition) A sterile batch cannot be dispositioned unless its sterility-assurance evidence chain is complete and reviewed: passing sterilisation/depyrogenation records for all product-contact items and their hold times, passing post-use filter integrity (and PUPSIT unless QA-justified), EM and personnel monitoring results for all sessions, the filling line and all aseptic operators holding valid APS/gowning qualification on the fill date, all interventions reviewed, 100% visual inspection and CCI results, and sterility/endotoxin results (or authorised parametric release).
why: Sterility cannot be tested into a batch; Annex 1 and the FDA aseptic guidance expect these records to be reviewed as part of batch release.
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapters 7-10; 21 CFR 211.113(b), 211.167(a), 211.192; FDA Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing guidance (2004) batch record review section

rule: (Tablets edition) Periodic IPC failures or missed checks during compression, coating or packaging automatically put the output produced since the last passing check on hold at container level (containers are time-stamped and IDs recorded), so the affected quantity is traceable and cannot be merged with good output before QA disposition.
why: In-process controls exist to detect drift during the run; without container-level segregation a failing check cannot be connected to the product it represents.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)-(c), 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 5

item: Approval routes (workflows) for MBRs, library elements, master data and batch record review
notes: Customers configure the number of stages, roles, parallel/serial order and escalation, but the engine always enforces the regulatory minimum: author != independent checker, quality-unit approval for masters and dispositions, QP certification in EU. Routes are versioned configuration under change control.

Role names and permission bundles are configurable (e.g. operator, verifier, supervisor, MBR author, QA reviewer, QP, planner). Hard constraints: segregation rules (admin vs GMP roles; performer vs verifier), no shared accounts, training prerequisites evaluated at action time, role changes audit-trailed and approved.

item: Signature requirements per step beyond the regulatory minimum
notes: Authors may add witness/verification, supervisor sign-off, or QA sign-off to any step and choose signature meanings from a controlled list. They cannot remove mandatory verifications (manual charge-in, manual yield calculation, critical manual data entry) or weaken e-signature authentication.

Targets, alert/action and acceptance limits, tiered relative-to-mean limits, precision and rounding policy per limit (USP or Ph. Eur. convention), and which limits block vs create exceptions (exception creation itself is not optional). Limits should come from versioned specifications (ideally synchronised from the product specification/LIMS) rather than typed into each MBR.

item: Forms, custom fields and step layouts
notes: Custom fields on steps and entities (batch, material lot, equipment, sample) with types, units, value sets and validation; screen layouts and grouping; help text and images. Custom fields that hold GMP data inherit audit trail, versioning and signature rules automatically; configuration cannot mark a GMP field as non-audited.
Formats for batch numbers, MBR IDs, sample IDs, container IDs, deviation references. Engine guarantees uniqueness and non-reuse, including for voided records.

Label templates (container/status/sample/dispensing labels), batch record report layouts and certificates. Templates are versioned and approved; data fields bind to record data (no free typing of GMP data on labels); report configuration cannot drop mandatory content from the complete-record export.
UI languages, MBR text translations (approved with the MBR version), date/number display formats, time zone display per site. Storage stays canonical (UTC, canonical numbers, unit codes).

item: Units of measure catalogue and conversions
notes: Customer can add units and conversion factors within dimensional classes (mass, volume, pressure, force, etc.), e.g. kp to N, based on a standard catalogue such as UCUM/SI; new conversion factors are verified and approved as configuration; dimensionally invalid conversions are impossible.

item: Master data models (materials, equipment classes, rooms, test methods, specifications)
notes: Classes, attributes, status models, qualification/calibration intervals, cleaning types and hold times, room grades, instrument types. Status gating behaviour is engine-defined; the customer defines which statuses exist beyond the mandatory ones (e.g. released/quarantine/rejected for materials; clean/dirty/in use/maintenance for equipment).

item: Exception taxonomy, severity proposals and routing
notes: Additional exception categories, default severity proposals, who is notified, which categories let the operator continue, QMS integration mapping. The mandatory exception types and the rule that open exceptions block disposition are not configurable; classification as deviation is a recorded QA decision.
Extra review checkpoints (production, QA, QP), additional exception types to surface, audit-trail review scopes beyond critical data, review checklists. The mandatory exception set cannot be reduced.

item: Time limits and hold times values
notes: All durations (mixing, drying, binder hold, dirty/clean hold, bulk hold, compounding-to-filtration, sterile hold, fill-to-lyo) are configured per product/equipment with a reference to the supporting validation/hold-time study; enforcement mechanism (server-time measurement, exception on breach) is fixed.

Sample sizes, locations, time/event triggers, test assignments and LIMS mappings per product; tablets: compression/coating/packaging IPC schedules per side/layer; injectables: EM plans, fill-weight check frequency, sterility sampling points, AQL plans.

Which scales, testers, presses, lyophilisers, sterilisers, EMS/BMS, LIMS, ERP, QMS, DMS, training and serialisation systems are connected and their tag/field mappings. Each interface is qualified; fallback-to-manual behaviour is defined per MBR but always flagged and verified.

item: Site/variant parameter sets (generic MBR + product parameters)
notes: Product-, strength-, pack- or market-specific parameters bound to a generic MBR (PAS-X GMBR style / ISA-88 site/master recipe split), e.g. tooling set, tablet weight, coating weight gain target, fill volume, lyo recipe ID, label artwork per market. Parameter sets are versioned and approved; they can only set declared parameters, not change structure.

item: Dashboards, notifications and operator UI preferences
notes: Non-GMP presentation features (worklists, KPIs, alerts, colour themes, per-user remembered filters). Low process risk under CSA-style assurance; must not hide mandatory prompts or exceptions.

Which curricula, SOP versions or qualifications (incl. injectables gowning/APS, visual inspector, tablets press operator) are required per step, MBR, room or equipment; read-and-understand triggers on new MBR versions. The check itself happens at action time and blocks when unmet.

item: Security policy parameters above regulatory floors
notes: Password length/complexity/expiry, MFA, session timeout, lockout thresholds, re-authentication frequency for signatures, SSO integration. Floors (two-component signatures, unique IDs, lockout after repeated failures) are fixed.

text: A safe customer formula language should be non-Turing-complete, side-effect free, guaranteed to terminate, statically typed and embeddable, with the host supplying the only functions and data it can see. Google's Common Expression Language (CEL) is a mature open-source example with exactly these properties (linear-time evaluation, no mutation, gradual typing, implementations in Go/Java/C++/Python); it is a reasonable base, extended with unit-aware quantity types and a closed pharma function library.

Use decimal, not binary floating-point, arithmetic for GMP calculations: binary doubles cannot represent values like 0.1 exactly, so results at a rounding boundary (e.g. 99.45 vs limit 99.5) can flip. OMG DMN's FEEL expression language defines its number type on IEEE 754-2008 decimal128 (34 significant digits), a precedent for business-rule languages; a pharma engine should adopt decimal128-class precision internally and make rounding mode explicit (note IEEE/many libraries default to round-half-even, whereas USP/Ph. Eur. comparisons need round-half-up).

Units of measure: represent every quantity as (decimal value, unit code) using a standard, machine-readable unit system such as UCUM, whose semantics rest on dimensional analysis (each unit = factor x vector of base-unit exponents), allowing automatic conversion between commensurable units and rejection of incommensurable operations at design time. Add pharma-specific semantic tags on top of dimensionless units (% w/w, % label claim, % LOD, % yield, counts of tablets/vials) so that, e.g., a % LOD is never added to a % yield even though both are dimensionless.

Precision model recommended (derived from USP General Notices 7.20 and Ph. Eur. General Notices): store raw values at acquired precision; carry full precision through all intermediate steps; attach a rounding rule (decimal places or significant figures, half-up) to each limit/specification and apply it only when forming the reportable value compared with that limit; store raw and reportable values; display intermediates rounded but never feed a displayed rounded value back into calculations.

Dependency graph (domain knowledge, spreadsheet-engine pattern): treat all calculations in an MBR as a directed acyclic graph of named values; detect cycles and unresolved references at design time; evaluate in topological order at run time as inputs arrive; when an input is corrected, recompute dependents, keep the superseded results in the record, and flag any dependent that was already signed/verified for re-verification. Store a calculation trace (expression version, input values with units and sources, output) for every computed value.

Compendial statistics and acceptance procedures (e.g. uniformity of mass tier rules, uniformity of dosage units acceptance value, friability three-run mean, dissolution stages, AQL acceptance numbers) should be delivered as vendor-validated library functions with fixed, versioned definitions (sample vs population SD, n-1 denominator, constants), not re-implemented by each customer formula; customers choose and parameterise them. This keeps high-risk logic in the Category-4 validated platform and out of per-MBR configuration.

Formula verification as part of MBR approval (domain knowledge): each customer expression should carry designer-supplied test vectors (normal values, limit edges including rounding boundaries, missing inputs, zero/negative guards) that the designer executes automatically; the pass/fail results are stored as objective evidence in the MBR verification report. Null/missing inputs and division by zero must yield an explicit error state that raises an exception, never a silent default of 0.

Time arithmetic for hold times and time limits must use UTC instants from the server clock so that daylight-saving changes and multi-site time zones cannot shorten or lengthen a measured hold time; display local time with the offset.

PharmaSuite's recipe designer has an expression editor whose data types let authors build conditions, rules and calculations with access to both definition-time and run-time information across the whole recipe, and Rockwell offers an SDK so partners/customers can build their own functional building blocks. Design implication: expose calculations and branching via a typed expression editor, but treat customer-built block types (SDK code) as Category 5 custom software with its own lifecycle, not as MBR configuration.

Industry practice for new eBRs is several rounds of prototype demonstrations and dry runs of the electronic MBR with end users before approval, then pilot batches with full QA review before go-live; this user-centred iteration is what prevents records that operators cannot execute without confusion. A configurable system should therefore make test executions cheap (sandbox/test mode on Draft masters, resettable test orders, simulated device inputs) and produce an MBR verification report from them.

'Paper on glass' (reproducing the paper record layout electronically with free-text fields and no integration to ERP/LIMS/automation) leaves data in digital silos and forfeits most eBR benefits (structured data, automatic checks, review by exception). ISPE guidance urges a data-centric rather than document-centric mindset. Design implication: the MBR designer should push authors toward typed blocks bound to master data and devices, and flag free-text capture of values that have structured blocks.

eBR projects have historically suffered long time-to-value and systems so complex to use and maintain that they are never fully rolled out; training before go-live and operator familiarity reduce unnecessary process exceptions that otherwise land on QA. Over-granular MBRs (a signature on every trivial action) create operator fatigue and exception noise; under-granular MBRs lose enforcement. Granularity should follow risk (CPPs/CQAs and GMP-required checks get enforced blocks; low-risk actions get grouped acknowledgements).

MBR verification package (recommended synthesis of FDA DI Q&A + CSA + GAMP 5): (1) automated static checks (completeness, plausibility, unit consistency, graph reachability, mandatory regulatory content); (2) formula test vectors executed by the designer; (3) risk-based test execution of the MBR in test mode covering every branch, loop exit, limit boundary and exception path of high-risk steps (scripted), plus exploratory walk-through by operators for usability (unscripted); (4) side-by-side review of the rendered MBR against the approved process description/registration; (5) author, independent checker and QA approval signatures. Library elements get the same treatment once and are then referenced, so per-MBR effort focuses on parameters and composition.

Two-tier validation model for a configurable eBR (GAMP 5 Category 4 platform + configured content): the vendor validates block types, the execution engine and guardrails once per release (leveraging supplier documentation/testing as GAMP 5 and CSA encourage), and the customer performs risk-based verification of the platform for their intended use plus verification of each MBR/library element as configuration. Anything that changes engine behaviour is a platform change (vendor release, full regression); anything that only composes blocks and sets parameters is an MBR change (MBR change control + verification package). The system should make this boundary technically explicit so every change self-classifies.

Regression across many configured MBRs after a platform upgrade is a known burden; mitigations: keep a library of automated test executions per block type and per representative MBR (golden batches with expected records), re-run them against each release in a validation environment, and compare generated records to expected outputs (including audit trail entries). PharmaSuite advertises preserving master data and batch records through documented 'evergreen' upgrades, indicating vendors treat upgrade continuity as a core requirement.

Configuration drift across sites: multi-site MES programmes use a versioned global template (core model) with standard building blocks and governed local variants; where a single global process template is impossible, shared building blocks plus a standard base application still preserve harmonisation. Treating templates as lifecycle-managed, versioned artefacts (with controlled branch/merge of site-specific changes back into the core) is what prevents drift and regressions. Design implication: ship a core library per edition, allow site libraries that extend but do not fork it, and report per-site divergence from the core version.

Scale: a complete record for one process can range from hundreds of pages with thousands of fields to thousands of pages with tens of thousands of fields. Performance design implications (domain knowledge): render and load the executed record incrementally per unit procedure/step rather than as one document; precompute exception indexes for review by exception; stream device/historian data as references plus summarised values instead of copying raw trends into the record; paginate audit trails; keep the approved MBR compiled into an immutable execution graph so record issuance and step transitions do not re-resolve libraries.

Where-used and version problems (domain knowledge): if MBRs reference library elements, master data or specifications 'by latest', an upstream change silently alters released masters (uncontrolled change); if they copy content, fixes do not propagate and MBRs diverge. The safe pattern is reference-with-version-pin plus a where-used index, impact assessment and a bulk 're-point and re-approve' workflow, with the executed record snapshotting all resolved versions.

Over-configurability that breaks compliance (synthesis): examples seen in configurable platforms include switches that bypass master approval for testing (Tempo), generic app builders where GMP semantics (verification, reconciliation, status checks) must be rebuilt by each customer (Tulip-style), and SDK/scripting escape hatches (PharmaSuite SDK). Each turns regulated behaviour into customer-owned logic that must be validated per use. The design rule: anything required by 21 CFR 211/Part 11/Annex 11/Annex 1 is an engine invariant; configuration only adds strictness or content.

MBR sprawl beyond packaging (domain knowledge): separate MBRs per strength, batch size, equipment train, market and language multiply change-control effort (one process change = dozens of MBR revisions). Mitigations: generic master + parameter sets (PAS-X GMBR), batch-size ranges with scaling rules, equipment classes instead of named units, market data (artwork, serialisation profile) as parameter sets, and translations inside the MBR version.

AI-assisted MBR authoring is arriving (Apprentice authoring agent converting PDFs to structured records; Siemens Opcenter Pharma 2605 AI-driven design of workflows, forms and checks). Generated MBR content must still pass the same static checks, test executions and author/checker/QA approvals; under the EU draft Annex 22 (July 2025) AI used in GMP needs defined intended use, validation and human oversight. Treat AI output as a draft authored by a named human who takes authorship responsibility.

ICH Q9(R1) (FDA final guidance May 2023; EMA effective 26 July 2023) addresses subjectivity and formality in quality risk management, clarifies risk-based decision-making and explicitly covers QRM in digitalisation and emerging technologies. It supports scaling MBR verification rigour to the risk of each step (formality proportional to risk) and documenting the rationale; ICH Q10 (FDA guidance 2009; EU GMP Part III) requires a change management system, which the MBR/library/configuration lifecycle must implement or integrate with.

Customisation beyond MBRs should follow one rule set across all configurable object types (custom fields, roles, workflows/approval routes, master data classes, label and report templates, UoM catalogue, numbering, languages): each is a versioned configuration item with author/approver, audit trail, effective dating, where-used, export/diff and promotion between environments (dev/test/validation/production) as a signed package. Vendors converge on this: Syncade automates transfer of recipes, material master data and configuration settings between environments; MasterControl keeps 'global elements' updated once and propagated.

Multi-site modelling can reuse ISA-88's general/site/master recipe layering: an edition-level core library (vendor), a company-level general recipe per product (process and formula, equipment-independent), a site recipe (local materials/suppliers, language, site time limits and EM plans), and a master recipe per equipment train/line. Changes flow downward via controlled re-approval; the executed record references all layers' versions.

Custom fields on core entities (batch, material lot, equipment, sample, exception) are a common customer need (e.g. customer-specific attributes, market codes). To stay compliant, a custom field declared as GMP data must automatically inherit audit trail, versioning, access control and inclusion in record exports; the configuration UI should not offer a 'non-GMP' flag for fields used in MBR logic, limits or labels.

Report/printout and label templates are high-visibility configuration: the complete batch record export, QA review report and certificates must include mandatory content defined by the engine (all data, signatures with manifestation, exceptions, audit trail links), so templates control layout and optional content only. Label templates bind fields to system data (status, lot, expiry, quantity) and are approved and versioned like MBRs, with artwork/market variants handled as parameter sets.

MasterControl Mx template builder: typed phase steps with step- and template-level settings for verification, access control and validation; data elements include single/multi-select, timestamps and step-complete; a 'phase projections' property displays a value entered elsewhere in the record wherever needed, avoiding re-entry (a single-source-of-truth pattern that a configurable eBR should adopt instead of duplicate data entry). MasterControl also launched an AI 'Master Template Generator' (beta) that converts paper batch records or natural-language instructions into draft templates.

Apprentice Tempo branching and calculations: conditional step navigation routes the operator to one of several steps via if/then/else rules on the previous step's result; automatic step execution can run calculations or equipment scans; formula outputs can be computed from multiple custom-property inputs and drive branching on equipment readings; exceptions are configurable per exception type (critical value, process issue, non-conformance) with real-time review routing.

GMP adaptation of ISA-88 control-recipe editing (domain knowledge): ISA-88 allows operators to modify a control recipe, but in a GMP eBR any run-time change to parameters must be constrained to ranges pre-approved in the master (e.g. proven acceptable ranges), be attributable, optionally verified, and be visible at review; structural changes (adding/removing steps) are never made in the control recipe and require a deviation or a new master version.

Equipment modelling (ISA-88 physical model: enterprise, site, area, process cell, unit, equipment module, control module) should back the MBR's equipment requirements: MBR steps request an equipment class with capability constraints at unit level; the engine binds actual units at execution and checks their status. This also enables one MBR to run on alternative trains and underpins the tablets edition (press/coater classes) and injectables edition (filling line, isolator, lyophiliser classes).

name: Sub-batch split and merge (genealogy)
purpose: Split a batch into sub-lots (e.g. several granulation sub-batches, several lyophiliser or steriliser loads, several packaging runs) and merge sub-lots into one downstream batch, keeping full genealogy.
config_options: allowed split/merge points in the flow
maximum number of sub-lots and naming rule
rules for merging (all sub-lots must be released/passed IPC, same MBR version, within hold time)
quantity allocation and reconciliation per sub-lot
engine_enforced_rules: every sub-lot has its own ID, record section and quantities; genealogy links are system-generated
merge is blocked if any sub-lot has open exceptions, failed IPC or expired hold unless QA dispositions
sub-lot quantities reconcile to the parent batch
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.188(b), 211.103, 211.111; EU GMP Chapter 4 and Chapter 5

name: Tablet visual defect inspection (AQL/sorting)
purpose: Inspect compressed or coated tablets for visual defects (chipping, capping, sticking, colour/coating defects, foreign tablets) by AQL sampling or 100% sorting.
config_options: defect catalogue and classes (critical/major/minor)
AQL sampling plan or 100% sorting mode (manual/automated)
acceptance numbers per class
action on failure (re-inspection only via approved procedure)
engine_enforced_rules: defect counts by class recorded per sample; acceptance evaluated by the engine
foreign tablet findings are critical and always raise an exception (possible mix-up)
rejected tablets feed reconciliation
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110, 211.192; EU GMP Chapter 5

name: Cleanroom/zone release for aseptic operations
purpose: Release a Grade A/B zone for aseptic processing: completion of cleaning/disinfection (incl. sporicide rotation), pressure cascade and airflow status, non-viable monitoring status, and room/line clearance.
config_options: disinfection programme reference (agents, rotation, contact times) per room
required status inputs (BMS pressure cascade, UDAF/HEPA status, particle counter status)
room clearance checklist for aseptic areas
validity period of a room release
engine_enforced_rules: aseptic steps cannot start in a zone without a valid release; BMS/EMS alarms during the session become exceptions
disinfection records carry agent lot/expiry and are verified
room release validity expires automatically (server time) and must be renewed
regulatory_basis: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) chapters 4, 6 and 9 (premises, cleaning/disinfection, monitoring); 21 CFR 211.42(c)(10), 211.56, 211.113(b)

text: PAS-X, Syncade, PharmaSuite and Opcenter test/simulation features for MBR verification (e.g. test orders on unreleased MBRs, simulation of device inputs, status names in the MBR lifecycle) could not be confirmed from public pages (vendor sites were blocked from this environment); confirm with vendor documentation or demos before copying their lifecycle model.

Should the two editions (tablets, injectables) share one validated compliance kernel (audit trail, e-signature, calculation engine, status checks, exception/RBE engine) with edition-specific block libraries, or be fully separate code bases? Separate kernels double validation effort and risk guardrail divergence; the scope change says 'independent products' but does not say whether code may be shared.

Which pharmacopoeia rounding convention applies per customer/product (USP vs Ph. Eur., or registration-specific)? The engine needs a per-specification rounding policy; confirm whether both must be supported in each edition and whether registered specifications ever deviate from compendial rounding.

For the injectables edition, how should PUPSIT 'not applicable' be modelled: Annex 1 section 8.87 permits alternative approaches only where justified by QRM; confirm with QA whether the MBR may carry a PUPSIT waiver referencing a risk assessment, and who approves it (QA only, or QA plus QP).

Is support for US OTC products without expiry dating (211.137 exemption, affecting retention periods under 211.180(a)) and for investigational (clinical) batches (EU Annex 13 / Regulation 536/2014 context, 21 CFR 210.2(c) phase 1 exemption) in scope? Both change record retention, labelling and blinding requirements for the tablets and injectables editions.

Will the editions integrate with an external EMS/LIMS/QMS/training system of record, or must they provide minimal built-in versions? Several engine guardrails (training check at action time, EM results blocking disposition, deviation closure blocking release) depend on reliable, validated interfaces.
